options.r: Money helps for a week, and then the tiredness comes back.

options.t: I'd ignore it. Everyone is tired in the last weeks of a project, and the launch is more important now. Nobody on the team can fix it before the launch day. A good party for the team will help.
options.c: Игнорирует людей.
options.r: One developer makes a serious mistake that costs three days.

steps.explain: Усталой команде нужны разгрузка и признание, а не только обещания отдыха позже или премии.

words.ex: Two developers show signs of burnout.

endings.good: You saved a failing project. The client renews, the team is proud, and the agency even makes a profit.
endings.mid: The project survives, but it costs the agency money and a lot of energy. You learn how early the signs of trouble appear.
endings.bad: The project fails, the client leaves, and two people leave the team. You remember this case in every new project.

steps.msg: You manage a program of five connected projects for one client. Hannah asks for a one-page roadmap for the steering committee. You have 40 pages of plans.

options.t: One page, three layers: quarters across the top, the five projects as bars, and key milestones as diamonds. I mark two cross-project dependencies and one risk in red. The detail stays in an appendix, and I'll send a draft by tomorrow so you can check the story.
options.c: Три слоя, зависимости и риск, детали в приложении: комитет видит программу целиком.

options.t: I'll send the 40 pages with a short cover note, so nothing is missing.
options.c: 40 страниц никто не прочитает.

options.t: I'll make one slide per project, five slides in total.
options.c: Пять слайдов не показывают связей между проектами.

options.t: I'll write a text summary of every project in a single page.
options.c: Текст не показывает сроки и зависимости.

words.how: Группа руководителей, которая принимает ключевые решения по программе.

words.ex: Mark each milestone with a diamond.

steps.msg: Project B cannot start testing until Project A delivers the login module. Project A's PM says it will be 'about two weeks late.' Both projects are in your program.

options.t: Thanks. Could you tell me the new date and what drives the delay? I'll ask B to start with the parts that don't need login, and I'll update the program plan today. Let's meet on Thursday to confirm, and I'll warn the steering committee if the date moves again.
options.c: Новая дата, причина, обходной путь для B и обновление плана: зависимость управляется.

options.t: Can you try to fix it faster? B is waiting for you.
options.c: Давление на A без анализа не ускорит работу.

options.t: I'll tell B's PM to wait until A is ready.
options.c: Ожидание без плана: B теряет две недели.

options.t: I'll ask B to move the testing two weeks, and we'll adjust.
options.c: Сдвиг B без поиска вариантов: цепная задержка.

words.how: Отдельная часть системы, которую можно разрабатывать отдельно.

words.ex: Project B is downstream of A.

words.how: Последствия одного сдвига для других работ.
words.ex: The delay has a ripple effect on testing.

steps.msg: The COO, Ava, asks for a short monthly report on the program. She says: 'I want to know three things: are we on track, what are the risks, what do you need from me?'

options.t: Subject: Program update, May. 1. On track: yes for four projects, one yellow. 2. Top risks: payment vendor delay, client approvals. 3. I need from you: a call with the vendor's executive this week. Full detail is attached if you want it.
options.c: Три ответа на три вопроса в первых строках, детали во вложении.

options.t: Subject: Program update. Please see the attached 12-page report.
options.c: Длинный отчёт не отвечает на три вопроса Авы.

options.t: Subject: Update. Everything is going well, and there's nothing for you to do.
options.c: «Всё хорошо» без фактов: ни доверия, ни действий.

options.t: Subject: Update. There are many problems, and we need your help.
options.c: Тревога без конкретики не даёт Аве действовать.

words.ex: Full detail is in the attachment.

words.how: Конкретная помощь, которую нужна от руководителя.
words.ex: My ask is a call with the vendor.

steps.msg: The program is 8% over budget for the first half. Paul says the CFO wants a clear explanation and a forecast for the full year.

options.t: The overrun has three sources: 3% from a vendor price increase, 3% from two approved change requests, and 2% from rework. If we don't act, I forecast 6% over for the year. With two corrective actions, a rate renegotiation and a stricter change process, we can bring it to 3%. I'll send a one-page variance report today.
options.c: Разложение отклонения по источникам, прогноз на год и корректирующие меры.

options.t: The program is over budget because of unexpected costs, and we're working on it.
options.c: «Непредвиденные расходы» не объяснение.

options.t: I'll ask the team to reduce hours and recover the budget.
options.c: Сокращение часов ударит по качеству и срокам.

options.t: The overrun is small. I'd wait until the next quarter to see what happens.
options.c: Ожидание не меняет цифр: CFO требует прогноза.

words.how: Разница между планом и фактом расходов.
words.ex: The budget variance is eight percent.

words.how: Прогноз итоговой стоимости на момент проверки.
words.ex: Our EAC is six percent over.

words.how: Шаг, чтобы вернуть проект к плану.

steps.msg: A new client program has many stakeholders: the CEO, marketing, IT, legal and two regional offices. Ava asks how you will manage their expectations.

options.t: I'll map them by influence and interest. High influence and high interest: the CEO and marketing, weekly contact. IT and legal: gatekeepers, involved early because they can block us. Regional offices: monthly updates and a named contact. I'll review the map every month, as positions change.
options.c: Карта по влиянию и интересу и разные ритмы общения; пересмотр раз в месяц.

options.t: I'll send everyone the same weekly report, so nobody feels left out.
options.c: Одинаковый отчёт всем: шум для одних и недостаток для других.

options.t: I'll focus on the CEO. If the CEO is happy, the others will follow.
options.c: Игнорирование юристов и ИТ может остановить проект.

options.t: I'll wait until someone has a problem, and then I'll respond.
options.c: Реакция вместо управления.

words.how: Человек или группа, на которых влияет проект.
Таблица для планирования общения со сторонами.
words.ex: I use an influence and interest grid.

words.how: Тот, кто может блокировать или разрешить работу.

steps.msg: You interview a PM candidate. Her CV is strong, but when you ask about a failed project, she says: 'That was the client's fault.' You want to know more.

options.t: Thank you. Let me ask it differently: if you could go back to week one of that project, what would you do differently? And what did you learn from it?
options.c: Открытый вопрос про неделю один и урок: проверяет рефлексию без обвинения.

options.t: I see. Clients can be difficult. Let's move on to the next question.
options.c: Пропуск сигнала: важный вопрос о зрелости остаётся без ответа.

options.t: Don't you think that a good PM should manage the client?
options.c: Риторический вопрос звучит как упрёк.

options.t: So you never make mistakes?
options.c: Сарказм портит интервью.

words.how: Вопрос про прошлый опыт, чтобы оценить поведение.
words.ex: Ask a behavioural question about failure.

words.how: Готовность отвечать за свою часть результата.
words.ex: I look for accountability in a candidate.

words.how: Способность разобрать прошлый опыт и сделать вывод.

steps.msg: A key vendor wants to change the contract: a longer notice period and no refund if the program is cancelled. Your program may change direction next year.

options.t: I'd accept the longer notice only if there is a partial refund for work not started, and a cancellation fee that decreases each quarter. I'd ask Legal to review it and send a counter-proposal this week. A vendor who wants a long relationship should accept a fair exit.
options.c: Условия обмена на возврат и снижающуюся плату: сбалансированный встречный запрос.

options.t: I'd accept it. The vendor is important, and we shouldn't lose them.
options.c: Принимать односторонние условия при неопределённости: риск.

options.t: I'd refuse any change. The old contract is fine.
options.c: Отказ ставит под угрозу отношения.

options.t: I'd sign it now, and ask Legal later.
options.c: Юрист потом: обязательства уже будут подписаны.

words.how: Время, за которое нужно предупредить о расторжении.
words.ex: The vendor wants a 90-day notice period.

words.how: Ответ на условия с вашими изменениями.
words.ex: Send a counter-proposal to the vendor.

steps.msg: Ava says: 'The program is on time and on budget, but the client's CEO asks what business value it gives. Can you show something?' You measure only delivery.

options.t: Good question. I'll ask the client for three business goals, such as faster order processing and fewer support calls. I'll record the baseline now and measure the same numbers after launch, so we can show the before and after. I'll bring a first draft at the next steering committee.
options.c: Цели клиента, базовые значения до запуска и измерение после: польза доказывается данными.

options.t: The program delivers all the features that were agreed. That is the value.
options.c: Выполнение требований не равно ценности для бизнеса.

options.t: I'll ask marketing to write a nice story about the benefits.
options.c: История без данных не убедит директора.

options.t: It's too early to measure benefits. We should wait for a year.
options.c: Если не собрать базу сейчас, потом сравнивать будет не с чем.

words.how: Управление тем, чтобы проект принёс бизнес-эффект.

words.ex: Faster orders is the main KPI.

steps.msg: Five PMs in your program make decisions in different ways. Dates, statuses and risks look different in every report. Hannah asks you to fix it.

options.t: I'll propose one page of rules: same status colors, one risk format, one reporting day, and one escalation path. We test it for a month with all five PMs, take their comments, and then make it final. The rules will serve them, not control them.
options.c: Короткие правила, месяц пилота и обратная связь: стандарт, который примут.

options.t: I'll send a template and ask everyone to use it from next week.
options.c: Шаблон без обсуждения часто игнорируют.

options.t: I'll review each report and correct the errors myself.
options.c: Ручные правки отнимают время и ничему не учат.

options.t: Each PM is an adult. Let them use their own way.
options.c: Без стандартов отчёты нельзя сводить.

words.how: Правила, роли и процессы принятия решений.
Кому и в каком порядке передавать проблему.

steps.msg: The client's CFO asks you to remove testing from the plan to save two weeks. He says: 'Our own team will test it later.' You see that this puts the program at risk.

options.t: I understand the need to save time. If we remove our testing, a defect found later costs about five times more to fix and may delay the launch. I can offer a shorter testing window of one week, focused on payments and login, and your team can run acceptance testing in parallel. Would that save enough time?
options.c: Понимает цель, объясняет цену дефекта и предлагает сокращённый, но целевой вариант.

options.t: I can't remove testing. It's part of our standard.
options.c: Отказ без альтернативы остановит разговор.

options.t: Okay, if you take the responsibility, we remove it.
options.c: Снять ответственность на словах не защитит программу.

options.t: We'll reduce testing, but quietly, so it doesn't look like a risk.
options.c: Скрытое сокращение: нечестно.

words.how: Проверка того, что новые изменения не сломали старое.
Проверка клиентом, что результат соответствует требованиям.
Больше проверок там, где выше риск.

steps.msg: At the steering committee, a client director says: "Your program has been yellow for three months. Why should we believe it will be green?" The room is quiet.

options.t: You are right to ask. Yellow stayed because of two causes: the vendor's delay and slow approvals. Both are now handled: a new vendor date, and a 48-hour approval rule. If we are not green by July 1, I will bring a recovery plan to this committee.
options.c: Признаёт, называет причины и условие.

options.t: The program has been yellow because it is complex. We are making progress, and I'm confident that it will be green soon.
options.c: Общие слова.

options.t: Yellow is not red. We are still within the budget and the date, and this status is normal for a program of this size.
options.c: Защищает статус.

options.t: I'd rather not go into details here. I'll write to you after the meeting with all the information. The room is not the right place. I need to check some numbers first. I would also like to discuss it with Ava.
options.c: Откладывает.

words.ex: Two root causes kept the program yellow.

words.how: Условия, при которых статус становится зелёным.

steps.msg: A director adds: "We want a decision today. Should we cut scope, add budget, or move the date?" You are asked to recommend one.

options.t: I recommend cutting scope: moving the reporting module and two small features to phase two. It keeps the date and the budget, and the loss for users is small. I can show the effect on one slide.
options.c: Одна рекомендация с обоснованием.

options.t: Maybe a mix of the three: a small budget increase, some scope change, and a one-week date move. It's more balanced.
options.c: Размывает решение.

options.t: It depends on what is more important for you: time, money or features. I'm ready to follow your choice.
options.c: Возвращает вопрос комитету.

options.t: I'd prefer not to recommend. The committee knows the business, and any option will be possible for us. I'd prefer not to choose between the options. All of them can work if we are careful. Our team can adapt to any of them.
options.c: Отказывается.

words.how: Короткий материал с вариантами и рекомендацией.

words.ex: A scope cut keeps the date.

words.how: Часть работы, перенесённая на следующий этап.
words.ex: The reports move to phase two.

steps.msg: Your program needs the client's IT department to open access to a server. IT says: "Next quarter." Your launch is in six weeks. Nobody at IT answers your emails.

options.t: Hi Tomas, I know your team is busy. The access blocks our launch in six weeks, and the client's CFO follows it. Can we have 15 minutes tomorrow to see what is the smallest step? I can prepare everything on our side.
options.c: Вежливо называет важность и просит короткий шаг.

options.t: Hi Tomas, please open the access as soon as possible, because it is an urgent request, and it blocks the whole program. The team has been waiting for three days. I wrote the request in the project channel.
options.c: Срочность без помощи.

options.t: I'll ask the client's CFO to tell IT to do it. He has the authority, and it is the fastest way.
options.c: Эскалирует сразу.

options.t: I'll wait until next quarter. IT has their own plan, and I don't want to create conflict with them.
options.c: Принимает срыв.

words.ex: Our sponsor can help with priority.

steps.msg: Tomas replies: "We can do it in three weeks if you send a security form first. The form is 12 pages." You see that the form needs input from your client's legal and your own IT.

options.t: Thank you, Tomas. I'll prepare the form this week: I'll fill what I can, and book 30 minutes each with our IT and your legal team. I'll send you the draft by Friday, and you tell me what is missing.
options.c: Берёт работу на себя и называет срок.

options.t: Thanks. I'll send the form to the relevant people and ask them to fill it in as soon as possible.
options.c: Раздаёт без контроля.

options.t: Twelve pages is a lot. Is there a shorter version? It's only a test server, and it doesn't need so much security.
options.c: Спорит с правилами.

options.t: Thanks. I'll ask the client's CFO to confirm that the form is not necessary in this case. He knows the client's rules better than I do. It saves me writing a long explanation. I'd attach our own summary.
options.c: Пытается обойти.

words.ex: The security review takes three weeks.

steps.msg: In a Monday review you see that the key project in your program is three weeks behind and will delay the whole launch. The client's CEO will speak at an event about the launch in six weeks. What do you do first?

options.t: I'd call the project PM and the lead developer, get the real picture in one hour, and prepare two or three options with costs. Then I'd call Ava and the client this week, not wait for the Friday report.
options.c: Реальная картина, варианты, быстрое сообщение.
options.r: Ava appreciates the early call, and the client hears about the delay from you first.

options.t: I'd ask the PM to catch up, and I'd review again next Monday. Three weeks may be recovered if the team works well.
options.c: Ждёт неделю.
options.r: The three weeks grow to four, and the client learns it from the status report.

options.t: I'd wait to tell the client until I have a perfect plan. Showing a problem without a solution would worry them. Last time I showed a half-ready plan, and the client lost trust. I'd take two more days.
options.c: Скрывает проблему.
options.r: The client discovers the delay at the Friday report and asks why you waited.

options.t: I'd tell the key project PM to add people from the other four projects now. This will solve the delay quickly.
options.c: Рушит остальные проекты.
options.r: The other four projects start to slip, and the PMs are angry with you.

steps.explain: Когда видите задержку ключевого проекта, быстро получите реальную картину, подготовьте варианты и сообщите руководителю и клиенту сразу.

words.how: О сроке: перенестись на более позднюю дату.
words.ex: The key project slips by three weeks.

words.how: Материал с вариантами, ценой и рекомендацией.

steps.msg: The options: (A) launch on time with 60% of the features; (B) launch three weeks late with all features; (C) launch on time with all features and add six developers at a cost of 90,000. Ava asks for your recommendation.

options.t: I recommend A with a public plan for the rest in the next release. The CEO can speak about a real working product on the event date, and the missing features follow within a month. I'd ask the client to confirm which 60%.
options.c: Рекомендация с планом и участием клиента.
options.r: Ava agrees to A, and the client starts to look at which features come first.

options.t: I recommend B. All features, and quality is safer. The event is important, but the CEO can talk about the product without the exact launch date.
options.c: Игнорирует событие.
options.r: The CEO misses the event date, and marketing is upset.

options.t: I recommend C. The budget is high, but we keep both date and scope. The agency can absorb part of the cost to keep the client happy. Option C is expensive, but it makes the client happy.
options.c: Дорого и рискованно: новые люди замедлят.
options.r: The budget doubles, and the new developers need weeks to catch up.

options.t: I'd show all three to the client and ask them to choose. It's their money and their event, so the decision is theirs.
options.c: Нет рекомендации.
options.r: The client decides slowly, and the event is only three weeks away.

steps.explain: Лидер программы приносит варианты с рекомендацией. Сокращение объёма с честным планом на остаток часто лучше, чем срыв даты или дорогое ускорение.

words.ex: A minimum viable launch is option A.
Option C needs a developer surge.
Publish a public roadmap for the rest.

steps.msg: The client's CEO says: "I don't like A. Marketing already promised all features on the event page." Marketing now wants you to join a call where they will blame the delay on the agency.

options.t: I'd join and stay calm. I'd say: "The delay is real, and we are fixing it. The promise on the page was made before the plan was confirmed by us, so let's agree how to update the page and use the event to show the first working release."
options.c: Признаёт часть, остаётся в фактах и предлагает выход.
options.r: The call stays calm, and marketing agrees to update the page.

options.t: I'd join, but I'd bring Ava with me so she can support us, and let her explain our position. Ava knows the client from earlier projects. I will prepare a short briefing for her. She is not afraid of difficult talks. Ava is good with this kind of client.
options.c: Прячется за руководителем.
options.r: Ava joins, but the client feels you are hiding behind her.

options.t: I'd refuse the call and send an email instead, because I don't want to be blamed in front of the client's team.
options.c: Избегает разговора.
options.r: The client says you avoid hard conversations, and trust falls.

options.t: I'd join and show them the emails where the promise was made without our approval. This protects us.
options.c: Нападает фактами.
options.r: The call becomes a fight, and the CEO hears only blame.

steps.explain: На созвоне с обвинениями держитесь фактов и решений. Признайте реальную часть проблемы и предложите, как использовать событие.

words.ex: We correct the record on the event page.

steps.msg: After the event, which went well with A, the client's CEO asks the agency to take over three more projects. Your team is full. Ava asks if you want to lead the new program. What is your answer?

options.t: Yes, and I'd ask for two things: a deputy PM for the current program, and a clear plan to hire two PMs by September. Without them I'd risk the quality of both programs.
options.c: Принимает и просит условия.
options.r: Ava agrees and sets up the deputy role, and your program stays healthy.

options.t: Yes, I'll do both. I'll work longer hours for a few months, and then we can find more help. I know it is a lot of work. I'm sure the team will understand.
options.c: Берёт всё на себя.
options.r: You work long hours, and by autumn both programs show problems.

options.t: I'd say no, because my team is exhausted, and I want to finish the current program properly. I'd suggest another PM for the new one.
options.c: Отказывается без обсуждения.
options.r: Ava gives the new program to another PM, and you lose a chance to grow.

options.t: Yes. It's a great chance, and the client trusts us. I'm sure that we can handle it without any change.
options.c: Игнорирует нагрузку.
options.r: The new programs start with no spare people, and quality drops within two months.

steps.explain: Перед новой работой назовите условия: заместитель и план найма. Согласие без условий часто ведёт к срыву обеих программ.

words.ex: I need succession for the current program.

endings.good: The program recovers and launches almost on time. You are known as a manager who sees problems early and shares them clearly.
endings.mid: The program launches late with a reduced scope. The client stays, but trust in your forecasts is lower.
endings.bad: The program fails, and the client cancels two of the five projects. The agency loses money, and you have to rebuild your credibility.

steps.msg: Hannah wants all PMs to move from spreadsheets to a new project management tool in one month. Several experienced PMs say: "Our spreadsheets work. Why change?"

options.t: Let's start with the why: fewer manual reports, one view of resources. I'd run a two-week pilot with three PMs who volunteer, collect their feedback, and then decide the rollout.
options.c: Объясняет «зачем» и запускает пилот.
options.r: The pilot gets three volunteers, and the other PMs follow their feedback.

options.t: Let's set a deadline. After one month, everyone uses the new tool and the spreadsheets are closed. People get used to change.
options.c: Приказ без объяснений.
options.r: Some PMs resist, and the new tool becomes a source of conflict.

options.t: I'd let each PM choose. If they have a good system, they can keep it, and we can see who gets better results. Each of them has a different way of working.
options.c: Нет общей картины.
options.r: Each PM uses their own system, and reports are different again.

options.t: I'd tell Hannah that it's a bad idea now, because we are in the middle of many projects, and change must wait.
options.c: Блокирует без аргументов.
options.r: Hannah says change cannot wait, and the tension grows.

steps.explain: Новые инструменты внедряют с объяснением выгоды и пилотом с добровольцами. Приказ или полная свобода одинаково слабы.

words.how: Подготовка людей к новому способу работы.
words.ex: Change management is half of the work.
Three volunteers form the pilot group.

steps.msg: During the pilot two PMs say the tool is slower than the spreadsheet for daily updates. One PM loves it. The data in the tool differs from the spreadsheets by 5%. What do you do?

options.t: I'd check the 5% first: find the cause and fix the import. Then I'd ask the two PMs what exactly is slow, and ask the vendor or the admin for shortcuts and templates. We repeat the test in a week.
options.c: Сначала данные, затем проблемы людей.
options.r: The PMs see that you take their problems seriously, and the next test is smoother.

options.t: I'd continue the pilot as it is. Some people will always say it's slower, but the benefits will be clear in a few months.
options.c: Игнорирует замечания.
options.r: The team reports the same problems again, and their trust falls.

options.t: I'd stop the pilot. The data is not right, and it could cause serious mistakes. Let's go back to spreadsheets.
options.c: Слишком резко.
options.r: The team goes back and sees that changes are not planned well.

options.t: I'd ask the PMs to enter data in both places during the pilot. This way we have a backup, and we can compare the numbers. It takes only five minutes more for each update.
options.c: Двойная работа и обида.
options.r: The PMs copy data twice and stop reporting the same day.

steps.explain: В пилоте сначала проверяйте качество данных, затем решайте проблемы удобства. Двойной ввод и игнорирование замечаний разрушают доверие.

words.how: Перемещение данных из старой системы в новую.
words.ex: The data migration has a 5% gap.

steps.msg: After three weeks, Hannah asks for a go or no-go decision on a full rollout. The results: reports are 30% faster, two PMs still prefer the old way. What do you recommend?

options.t: Go, with conditions: a three-month period where spreadsheets are read-only, a weekly help hour, and a review in month three. For the two PMs, a short one-to-one to understand their needs.
options.c: Решение с условиями и поддержкой.
options.r: Hannah accepts the plan, and two PMs agree to try for three months.

options.t: Go. The numbers are good, and we cannot wait for everyone to agree. After a while the two PMs will adapt.
options.c: Игнорирует двух сомневающихся.
options.r: The two PMs stay quiet but keep the old files on the side.

options.t: No-go. Two PMs are not happy, and I'd rather wait for the next quarter, when we have more time.
options.c: Откладывает без причины.
options.r: The decision slips to the next quarter, and the team feels uncertain.

options.t: Go, but only for new projects. The old ones can continue in spreadsheets until they are finished. Changing a running project is risky. The people there are already used to the old files.
options.c: Две системы надолго.
options.r: Some projects stay in spreadsheets for a year, and reports are hard to combine.

steps.explain: Решение о внедрении принимают с условиями и поддержкой: переходный период, часы помощи и разговор с сомневающимися.

words.ex: The full rollout starts in June.
We sunset the spreadsheets in three months.
Report time is the success metric.

endings.good: The team adopts the new tool without pain, and reports are better. People feel they helped to choose it.
endings.mid: The tool is used, but some people keep their own spreadsheets, and reports are mixed.
endings.bad: People refuse to use the new tool, and you lose a month of work and some trust.

steps.msg: Ava notes that projects at Atlas finish late 40% of the time. She asks you, the new Head of Delivery: 'What will you change first?' You have been in the role for two weeks.

options.t: I wouldn't change anything yet. For four weeks I'll review twenty finished projects and find the three most common causes of delay. Then I'll bring you one change for each cause, with a metric, an owner and a date, so we fix the system and not the symptoms.
options.c: Сначала данные: причины, потом по одному изменению на причину с метрикой и владельцем.

options.t: I'd introduce a mandatory planning checklist for every project.
options.c: Чек-лист без диагностики лечит неизвестную болезнь.

options.t: I'd replace the project managers whose projects are late most often.
options.c: Люди — следствие, а не причина: система не поменяется.

options.t: I'd add a 20% buffer to every project plan.
options.c: Ровный буфер скрывает причины и удлиняет сроки.

words.how: Процент проектов, завершённых в плановый срок.

words.ex: I run a root cause analysis on late projects.

words.how: Проблема процесса, а не отдельного человека.
words.ex: Late approvals are a systemic issue.

steps.msg: You want to track delivery quality, but the team has many numbers: hours, tickets, bugs, satisfaction. Paul says: 'Pick a few. Nobody will read fifteen metrics.'

options.t: Four: on-time delivery rate, margin per project, client satisfaction after launch (CSAT), and defects found by the client in the first month. One page, monthly, with a trend line and a short comment. Each metric has an owner and a target.
options.c: Четыре показателя: срок, маржа, удовлетворённость клиента, дефекты у клиента: баланс.

options.t: I'd track everything and let each manager choose what to read.
options.c: Все метрики: шум, которого не читают.

options.t: Only the profit. It's the one number that matters to the business.
options.c: Одна прибыль не покажет, почему она изменилась.

options.t: I'd track hours and tickets, because they are easy to measure.
options.c: Лёгкие метрики не отражают качество.

words.how: Оценка клиентом проекта, обычно после запуска.

words.ex: Late approvals are a leading indicator.

steps.msg: Dan, a project manager, has had two projects with unhappy clients in six months. He is hard-working and kind. You must tell him that his results are below the standard.

options.t: Dan, I want to be direct, because I want you to succeed. Two clients were unhappy, mainly about unclear communication. Your team likes you, and that's a real strength. Let's set three specific changes for the next quarter, such as a weekly status and a risk review, and meet every two weeks to check progress.
options.c: Прямота, факты, сильная сторона и три конкретных изменения с проверками.

options.t: Dan, you are a great person. But the clients were not happy. Let's try to do better.
options.c: Слишком мягко: причина и план неясны.

options.t: Dan, your performance is poor. If it doesn't improve in three months, we will need to talk about your future.
options.c: Угроза без помощи: Дэн потеряет мотивацию.

options.t: Dan, I'd like to move you to a smaller project where you will have fewer problems.
options.c: Решение за человека без разговора.

words.how: Формальный разговор о достижениях и проблемах.
words.ex: The performance review is on Friday.

words.how: Конкретные шаги и сроки для улучшения результата.
words.ex: We agree on an improvement plan.

steps.msg: Ava shows that one client brings 38% of revenue. If it leaves, the agency is in danger. She asks if the Delivery team can help reduce this risk.

options.t: Yes, in two ways. First, I'd secure the key client with a quarterly business review with their leadership. Second, I'd free two senior PMs to support new-client pitches and early projects. Target: below 25% from one client in 18 months.
options.c: Защищает ключевого клиента и освобождает сильных PM для новых: два пути с целью.

options.t: We can focus on delivering that client's projects even better.
options.c: Больше внимания одному клиенту усиливает зависимость.

options.t: Let's tell the client they are too big a part of our revenue.
options.c: Прямой разговор с клиентом о зависимости: странный.

options.t: I don't think Delivery can help. This is a sales problem.
options.c: Отказ от ответственности.

words.how: Встреча с клиентом: результаты и планы.
words.ex: We hold a quarterly business review.

steps.msg: Julia suggests changing from fixed price to time and materials for all projects. Clients often change scope, and fixed prices cost the agency money. You see pros and cons.

options.t: I'd use a mix: fixed price for clear, small scopes, and time and materials with a monthly cap for large or uncertain projects. We test it on five new projects and review the margin and client feedback in six months. This protects us and still gives clients a budget limit.
options.c: Смешанная модель с лимитом и пилотом на пяти проектах: управляемый эксперимент.

options.t: I'd agree. Time and materials is safer, so let's use it everywhere.
options.c: T&M везде отпугнёт клиентов с жёстким бюджетом.

options.t: I'd keep fixed price everywhere. Clients like certainty.
options.c: Фикс везде сохраняет текущую проблему.

options.t: I'd let each PM choose the model for each project.
options.c: Решения PM без правил дадут хаос.

words.w: time and materials with a cap
words.how: Клиент платит за фактические часы, но не больше установленной суммы.
words.ex: T&M with a cap suits uncertain scope.

words.how: Описание того, что входит в проект.
words.ex: Fixed price needs a clear scope definition.

words.how: Максимальная сумма, которую клиент готов потратить.
words.ex: The client wants a budget ceiling.

steps.msg: The Head of Design and the Head of Development both come to you. Design says developers ignore the designs. Development says designers hand over unrealistic files.

options.t: Both of you are right about the symptoms, and I'd like to fix the process. Let's run a pilot: a developer joins the design review, and a designer joins the technical review. We use a shared checklist for handoff, and we measure rework hours for two months. Can we agree on that today?
options.c: Признаёт обе стороны, предлагает пилот процесса, метрику и срок.

options.t: Let's ask the CEO to decide who is right.
options.c: Эскалация вместо решения.

options.t: I'll tell developers to follow the designs, and designers to make them simpler.
options.c: Односторонние указания не изменят процесс.

options.t: Let's not take sides. They need to solve this between themselves.
options.c: Нейтралитет без решения: конфликт останется.

words.ex: The handoff between design and dev is weak.

words.how: Повторная работа из-за ошибки или недопонимания.

steps.msg: Sales wants to sign a big contract with a very short deadline and a client with a bad reputation: they pay late and change requirements all the time. Julia asks for Delivery's opinion.

options.t: I'd sign only with protections: a 40% advance payment, a written change process, a named decision-maker on the client side, and a realistic date. If they don't accept, I'd walk away. The revenue is not worth a project that loses money and burns out the team.
options.c: Подписать только при защите: аванс, процесс изменений, ответственное лицо и реалистичная дата.

options.t: I'd sign it. A big contract is a big opportunity.
options.c: Подпись без защиты: большая сделка может стать убытком.

options.t: I'd refuse it. A client with a bad reputation is never worth it.
options.c: Отказ без обсуждения условий: теряет возможную сделку.

options.t: I'd sign it and add a higher price to cover the risk.
options.c: Цена не решает проблему поздних платежей и изменений.

words.ex: Shorten the payment terms to 15 days.
We are ready to walk away.

steps.msg: Your best Senior PM, Hannah, says she got an offer from another agency with 20% more pay. She says: 'I love it here, but I need to think.' She asks for your advice.

options.t: Thank you for telling me. I'd like to keep you. Let me check what I can offer within a week, such as a pay review, a bigger role, or a program to lead. What matters most to you? I'll also be honest: I can't promise to match every number, but I want to find the best offer we can make.
options.c: Признание ценности, срок на предложение, вопрос о приоритетах и честность об ограничениях.

options.t: It's a great offer. You should take it, and we'll be happy for you.
options.c: Слишком рано отпускает сильного сотрудника.

options.t: We can match the 20% increase, no problem.
options.c: Моментальное обещание без согласования.

options.t: I'm surprised. I thought you were happy here.
options.c: Упрёк: человек почувствует вину.

words.how: Ответ работодателя на предложение другой компании.

words.ex: She wants a clearer growth path.

steps.msg: Ava asks for the Delivery plan for next year. You need to include goals, a hiring plan and tools, with a budget that is 10% lower than this year.

options.t: Three goals: raise on-time delivery from 60% to 80%, raise margin from 22% to 26%, and keep turnover below 10%. Hiring: two PMs, none for design. Tools: one platform instead of three, which pays for itself in eight months. I'll show the budget by quarter and what we stop doing to save 10%.
options.c: Три измеримые цели, найм, инструменты и откуда экономия.

options.t: Goals: improve everything by 10%. Hiring: as needed. Tools: keep the current ones.
options.c: Общие слова без цифр.

options.t: I'd propose a plan with ambitious goals. If we aim high, we'll reach more.
options.c: Амбиции без бюджета нереалистичны.

options.t: I'd propose to keep the same plan as this year, because the budget is lower.
options.c: Копия прошлого года не отвечает на снижение бюджета.

words.how: Процент сотрудников, которые уходят за период.

words.ex: The new platform has a business case.

steps.msg: Dan did not improve after three months and you must end his contract. He has done his best, and he is a good person. Ava says: 'Please do it today.'

options.t: Dan, I have difficult news. We are ending your contract, effective in four weeks. I want to tell you why, and what happens next: pay, a reference, and help with finding a new role. I'm sorry. I know you worked hard, and I'm available to answer any questions.
options.c: Прямо, с датой, причинами, поддержкой и человечески.

options.t: Dan, I'm afraid your results didn't improve, so we have to let you go. Please finish the day.
options.c: Холодно и обрывисто: неуважение к человеку.

options.t: Dan, there is a possibility that we may need to review your contract soon.
options.c: Намёки вместо ясности: ложная надежда.

options.t: Dan, let's talk next week about your future with the company.
options.c: Откладывание при уже принятом решении.

words.how: Дата, с которой решение начинает действовать.
Время между решением и последним днём.
words.ex: He has a four-week notice period.

steps.msg: The CEO wants the agency margin to rise from 22% to 30% this year. Ava asks you if Delivery can do it. You know that it needs big changes.

options.t: Not in one year without hurting quality. I see 26% as realistic: better scoping, fewer free revisions, and less idle time. For 30% we would also need to raise prices and drop two unprofitable clients. I can show you the numbers.
options.c: Реальный уровень, условия для большего.

options.t: I'll try my best. We will look for savings everywhere, and I'm sure that we can get close to 30%. Some suppliers will give a discount if we sign early. I'd start with the office and the software. We will see the real number in a month.
options.c: Обещает без анализа.

options.t: 30% is not possible. The industry average is 25%, so the CEO's target is not realistic for a service business.
options.c: Отказ с обобщением.

options.t: Let's tell the team that the margin must go up, and each PM gets a target. They will find a way.
options.c: Перекладывает.

words.how: Угроза, что рост маржи ухудшит результат.
words.ex: A fast margin push is a quality risk.
There are three levers: scope, rates, utilization.

steps.msg: Ava says the CEO wants a 30% plan anyway: "Give me something I can show." You must find a way to be honest and useful at the same time.

options.t: I can show a two-year path: 25% this year, 28% next year, 30% in year three, with the actions for each step and a cost. This shows ambition and a realistic way. If the CEO wants more speed, I'd offer a pilot of the new pricing.
options.c: Двухлетний путь с шагами.

options.t: I'll prepare a 30% plan, but with a note that it depends on many things: prices, clients and hiring. It is not guaranteed.
options.c: Формально выполняет.

options.t: I'll write the 30% plan as asked. If it doesn't work, we can explain next year what happened and why. Some of the numbers are very difficult to reach. I will tell the board about the risks in the plan. It will be easier to speak after the first quarter.
options.c: Откладывает честность.

options.t: I'd ask Ava to talk to the CEO. The target is unrealistic, and I don't want to work on a plan that I can't believe.
options.c: Отказывается.

words.how: Цель, разбитая на шаги по годам.

words.ex: The board needs a credible plan.
I can't commit to 30% in one year.

steps.msg: A long-term client, Greg, writes an angry email to Ava and you: "Your new PM does not understand our business. We want a different PM or we reconsider our work with Atlas." The PM is Dan's replacement, six weeks in.

options.t: Dear Greg, thank you for telling us directly. I'd like to understand what is missing. Can I call you tomorrow, and meet the PM and you together next week? I'll share a plan after the call, and a different PM remains an option.
options.c: Слушает, назначает шаги и оставляет вариант замены.

options.t: Dear Greg, I'm sorry about your experience. I'll talk with the PM, and we'll improve. I hope you can give us a little more time.
options.c: Просит время.

options.t: Dear Greg, we will replace the PM immediately, and we are sorry for the problem. A new person will contact you tomorrow.
options.c: Заменяет без разбора.

options.t: Dear Greg, the PM is experienced and is doing everything correctly. I think it's only a matter of getting used to each other. The client's team has changed three times this year. A new group always needs a few months.
options.c: Не слышит жалобу.

words.ex: This is a serious relationship risk.

words.how: Не защищаться, пока не поймёте проблему.

steps.msg: On the call Greg says the PM asks too many basic questions about his industry. You check and the PM's questions were about payment rules, which are specific to the client's market. The PM has no industry training.

options.t: Thank you, that is clear. Our PM will do a two-day onboarding with your team on payment rules, and I'll add a client-industry briefing to our standard start. Can your team lead it? We review after four weeks.
options.c: Конкретное решение для клиента и процесса.

options.t: Thank you for the explanation. I'll ask the PM to read documents about your industry and come to the next meeting prepared.
options.c: Перекладывает обучение на PM.

options.t: The questions are part of a normal start. I'd suggest that your team prepares a short document about the rules, and we will use it.
options.c: Просит клиента сделать работу.

options.t: We'll replace the PM with someone who knows the industry, and that will take about a month. I'd also ask the client to join the interviews. The new PM would start in the next quarter.
options.c: Долго.

words.ex: We add a client briefing to the start.

steps.msg: In one week, three of your seven senior PMs resign. All three go to the same competitor. Ava asks: "How bad is this, and what do we do?" You have 24 hours.

options.t: It is serious: those three lead 11 of our 30 projects. In 24 hours I'll give you: the list of risks per project, a coverage plan, and talks with each remaining PM. I'd also ask the three for an honest exit interview.
options.c: Оценка, план и шаги за 24 часа.
options.r: Ava appreciates the numbers, and the coverage plan starts the next morning.

options.t: We will manage. I'll divide their projects between the other PMs and ask them to work a bit more for a month.
options.c: Делит нагрузку без анализа.
options.r: The remaining PMs get overloaded, and a fourth one starts looking for another job.

options.t: It's a big blow, but people leave in every company. Let's wait a few days and see if others also want to leave.
options.c: Ждёт.
options.r: Two more PMs leave during the waiting week, and clients start asking questions.

options.t: It's a betrayal. The three PMs should leave immediately, and we shouldn't let them talk to clients anymore. They have lost our trust. I'd say it in the next meeting with the whole team. Maybe we also need a new policy for contacts.
options.c: Эмоциональная реакция.
options.r: The team hears the anger and feels the atmosphere become tense.

steps.explain: Когда уходит часть команды, оцените масштаб в цифрах, составьте план покрытия за сутки и поговорите с остающимися. Эмоции мешают.

words.how: Беседа с сотрудником, чтобы он остался.
words.ex: I hold a retention talk with each PM.

steps.msg: In the exit interviews, two of the three say: "No career path, pay is behind the market, and the workload is uneven." You know that they are right on two of the three.

options.t: Thank you for being honest. Pay and workload: you're right, and I'll fix them. Career path: I'm working on a three-step model. I'll share what changes to the team in a week, so the people who stay see that it was not in vain.
options.c: Признаёт правду и обещает изменения.
options.r: The three leave with respect, and one gives you useful advice for the next hires.

options.t: Thank you for the feedback. We take it seriously, and we'll look at it when we have time.
options.c: Пустые слова.
options.r: The team hears nothing new, and people begin to doubt that anything will change.

options.t: Thank you. I think each of you had your reasons, and some of them may not be completely fair. Anyway, we wish you all the best. I know that it was not easy for you. I'd also write a recommendation letter for each of you.
options.c: Оправдывается.
options.r: The leavers defend themselves, and the interview becomes a debate.

options.t: I'm disappointed that you did not say it earlier. If you did, we could have solved it together.
options.c: Упрекает.
options.r: The leavers go silent and the useful details are lost.

steps.explain: Честный выход-интервью полезен, если вы признаёте верные замечания и показываете оставшимся, что изменения будут.

steps.msg: The four remaining Senior PMs meet you. One says: "We heard that you will hire from outside to fill the three roles. Why not promote us?" Two of them have asked about growth before.

options.t: It's a fair question. I'd like to promote from within. I'll open two of the three roles for internal applications, with clear criteria, and hire one external person with a specific skill. I'll share the criteria in a week and meet each of you.
options.c: Прозрачные критерии и повышение изнутри.
options.r: The four PMs see the criteria, and two apply for the open roles.

options.t: We will look at both options. Of course, internal candidates are very welcome, and we will see who is best for the roles. We have no preference. Inside candidates know the company, and the outside ones bring new ideas. We make the decision in the second round.
options.c: Неясные условия.
options.r: Nobody knows who will be hired, and two PMs start to look around.

options.t: External people bring new ideas. I think we need both, and I'll decide when I see the candidates.
options.c: Не отвечает на вопрос.
options.r: The PMs feel you avoid their question, and morale drops.

options.t: Please don't be impatient. We are in a hard time, and the roles will be filled soon. I'll tell you about my decision.
options.c: Отмахивается.
options.r: The PMs hear no real answer, and one resigns the next month.

steps.explain: Остающиеся ждут прозрачности. Дайте критерии, откройте часть ролей изнутри и поговорите с каждым.

words.how: Назначение сотрудника на более высокую роль.

words.ex: One role goes to an external hire.

steps.msg: Two weeks later a client says: "I heard that many PMs left. Is my project safe?" Ava asks you to answer him. How do you reply?

options.t: Yes, your project is safe. Your PM is staying, and we added a second person who knows the project. Three PMs left, and we took action: coverage plans for every project, and a new hiring plan. I'm available any time to talk.
options.c: Факты, защита и доступность.
options.r: The client feels safe and tells Ava that he values the honesty.

options.t: Yes, don't worry. Everything is under control, and the quality of work will remain the same. The clients will not feel any change. I have already talked to the leaders of the teams. We will keep the same standards.
options.c: Обещание без деталей.
options.r: The client does not believe the general words and asks for a call with Ava.

options.t: People leave from time to time in every agency. It doesn't affect your project in any way.
options.c: Отрицает проблему.
options.r: The client finds the truth online and doubts everything you say.

options.t: I can't comment on internal matters. If you have a problem with your project, please send me a message.
options.c: Уходит от ответа.
options.r: The client feels you hide something and starts to talk to other agencies.

steps.explain: Клиенту нужны факты: кто ведёт проект, что сделано для защиты и как с вами связаться. Отрицание или молчание вредят доверию.

words.how: Способность работать без сбоев при потерях.

words.ex: Each project has a named backup.

endings.good: You stabilize the team within three months. The remaining people feel heard, and clients see no big drop in quality.
endings.mid: Delivery recovers but with a few missed deadlines. The team is still careful and clients ask more questions.
endings.bad: More people leave, two clients complain, and the agency's reputation suffers.

steps.msg: At the board meeting Richard asks: 'Revenue grew 15%, but profit fell. Is this a one-time problem or a trend?' You have the numbers, and the answer is mixed.

options.t: Both. About a third is one-time: a large client's late payment and a lost pitch. Two thirds is a trend: salary growth and more rework. We act on the trend with two steps: a pricing review and a rework target. I'll bring the numbers by quarter next month.
options.c: Честное разделение на разовое и системное с мерами и сроком.

options.t: It's mostly a one-time problem. Next quarter will be better.
options.c: Оптимизм без данных: совет не поверит.

options.t: It's a trend, and it will continue unless we change the model.
options.c: Пессимизм без плана.

options.t: I'd like to take this question after the meeting, with the finance team.
options.c: Откладывание на совете выглядит как уход от ответа.

words.ex: The late payment is a one-off.
Salary growth is a structural issue.

words.how: Прибыль от основной деятельности как доля выручки.
words.ex: Operating margin fell by four points.

steps.msg: Ava, now the CEO, asks you to propose where Atlas should be in three years. The market is changing: clients ask for fixed prices, AI tools make some work faster, and big agencies buy smaller ones.

options.t: Three bets: first, specialize in two industries where we have cases; second, use AI to cut production time by 25% and sell outcomes, not hours; third, keep the team under 100 people so we stay close to clients. For each bet I'd show the investment, the risk and a first test in 90 days.
options.c: Три ставки: специализация, AI и размер; у каждой инвестиции, риск и тест за 90 дней.

options.t: We should grow as fast as possible and become a large agency.
options.c: Рост ради роста без ставки.

options.t: We should stay the same. Our model has worked for ten years.
options.c: Статус-кво при изменениях рынка рискован.

options.t: We should sell the company to a bigger agency before it's too late.
options.c: Продажа — отказ от стратегии, а не стратегия.

words.how: Клиент платит за итог, а не за часы.
Инвестиция с неопределённым, но важным результатом.

steps.msg: A small agency of 15 people wants to join Atlas. Ava asks you to lead the integration. The two cultures are different: they are informal, and Atlas has strict processes.

options.t: Before we sign I'd talk to their five key people and map three things: how they deliver, how they treat clients, and what they fear. Then I'd keep their client-facing style, and integrate only finance, tools and the delivery standard in the first six months. We review at day 100.
options.c: Сначала изучить, потом интегрировать только нужное и проверить на сотый день.

options.t: I'd move them to our processes in the first month. One company, one way.
options.c: Резкий переход ломает то, что делало их сильными.

options.t: I'd keep them separate and independent for two years.
options.c: Полная независимость — это не интеграция.

options.t: I'd ask Ava to decide what to keep and what to change.
options.c: Отказ от роли: Ава попросила вас вести.

words.ex: We run due diligence on delivery.

words.how: План объединения людей, процессов и систем.
words.ex: The integration plan has three phases.

words.how: Насколько совпадают ценности и стиль работы.

steps.msg: Revenue fell 20% after a big client left. Ava says: 'We must cut costs by 15%. I see two options: layoffs of ten people, or a pay cut for everybody.' She asks what you think.

options.t: I'd look at a third option first: freeze hiring, cut tools and office costs, and move people to billable projects. If we still need more, a small number of layoffs is better than a pay cut for everybody, and I'd do it once, clearly and fairly, with severance. I'll bring the model by Friday.
options.c: Сначала нелюдские меры, затем минимум сокращений, честно и один раз.

options.t: Layoffs. They're faster and cleaner than a pay cut.
options.c: Сокращение первым вариантом без анализа затрат.

options.t: A pay cut for everybody. It's fairer, and nobody loses a job.
options.c: Сокращение зарплат у всех ударит по сильным сотрудникам.

options.t: I'd wait for a quarter. Maybe we win a new client.
options.c: Ожидание при падении выручки на 20%.

words.ex: Redeployment to billable work saves cost.

steps.msg: An investor, Richard, wants a short update before the quarter ends. The quarter was weak. You know that his email will be forwarded to other investors.

options.t: Subject: Q3 update. Short version: revenue is down 8% and margin four points, because of one client loss. Three actions: a new pipeline with five pitches, a cost review, and a focus on two industries. Outlook: Q4 will be flat, and we expect to recover in Q1. I can call you any time this week.
options.c: Цифры, причина, три меры, прогноз и приглашение к разговору.

options.t: Subject: Q3 update. The quarter was a bit challenging but nothing unusual.
options.c: Смягчение без чисел: инвесторы увидят приукрашивание.

options.t: Subject: Q3 update. We had a terrible quarter, and we're working hard to fix it.
options.c: Эмоции без фактов.

options.t: Subject: Q3 update. I'll send you the report after the quarter ends.
options.c: Задержка при запросе до конца квартала.

words.ex: The outlook for Q4 is flat.
Results are in line with the forecast.
The client loss is a one-time impact.

steps.msg: Hannah tells you the team feels that leadership talks about work-life balance but sends emails at midnight. People copy this behavior.

options.t: She is right about me. I'll stop sending messages after 8 p.m., use scheduled send, and say it in the all-hands. I'll ask the other leaders to do the same, and we'll check it with a short pulse survey in three months.
options.c: Признаёт личный вклад, показывает пример, просит лидеров и проверяет опросом.

options.t: I send emails late because I like to work at night. It doesn't mean anyone must answer.
options.c: Оправдание: сотрудники читают сигнал, а не намерение.

options.t: I'll send a policy: no emails after 8 p.m. for everyone.
options.c: Политика без примера лидера не сработает.

options.t: People should manage their own boundaries. It's their responsibility.
options.c: Перекладывает ответственность на сотрудников.

words.ru: баланс между работой и личной жизнью
words.how: Разумная граница между работой и отдыхом.

words.ex: We run a pulse survey each quarter.

steps.msg: Ava asks whether to raise prices by 12%. Clients are price-sensitive, and two competitors cut their rates. The team is at 85% capacity.

options.t: I'd raise by 12% for new clients and 6% for current ones with a long relationship, announced 90 days ahead, with a clear reason. A team at 85% capacity tells me we have demand. We watch churn for six months, and if it rises above 5%, we review.
options.c: Дифференцированное повышение, срок уведомления и порог пересмотра.

options.t: I'd raise prices by 12% for everyone from next month.
options.c: Единое повышение сразу вызовет отток.

options.t: I'd keep the prices, since competitors are cutting.
options.c: Не повышать при загрузке 85% — потеря маржи.

options.t: I'd lower prices by 5% to win more clients.
options.c: Снижение цены при спросе — ошибка.

words.how: Клиент, для которого цена очень важна.
Способность повышать цену без потери клиентов.

steps.msg: Developers and designers use AI tools. Some clients ask: 'Do you use AI on our project, and do we pay less?' Hannah asks you to define the agency's policy.

options.t: A clear policy: we use AI when it improves quality or speed, we tell clients which tools and for what, we never put client data in public tools, and we price by results, not by hours. Speed gains go partly to the client and partly to investment in quality. I'll draft it this week.
options.c: Прозрачная политика: когда, где, что нельзя, и как делить выгоду.

options.t: We don't tell clients. AI is our internal tool, like a text editor.
options.c: Скрывать использование: вопрос доверия и безопасности.

options.t: We refuse to use AI on client projects. It's too risky.
options.c: Отказ — потеря скорости и клиентов.

options.t: We use AI everywhere and charge the same price. The clients pay for the result.
options.c: Цена без объяснения вызовет конфликт.

words.ex: Never put client data in public tools.

words.how: Открытое сообщение клиенту о том, что и как мы делаем.

steps.msg: Ava plans to step back in two years and says you are a candidate for CEO. But she asks: 'What would you need to prepare, and what worries you?' You have not been the CEO before.

options.t: I need more experience in sales, finance and board work, where I know less. I'd ask for a six-month rotation with sales and regular board preparation with Paul. My concern is that I may protect delivery too much and underweight growth. Could you challenge me on that regularly?
options.c: Конкретные пробелы, план подготовки и просьба о честной обратной связи.

options.t: I don't need to prepare. I know the company better than anyone.
options.c: Самоуверенность: Ава увидит пробелы.

options.t: I'm not sure I want this job. I enjoy delivery more.
options.c: Уклонение от вопроса без решения.

options.t: My only concern is that other candidates may be better than me.
options.c: Тревога без плана.

words.ex: The CEO has a succession plan.
A rotation in sales builds experience.

steps.msg: A client posts on social media: 'Atlas delivered a broken site and does not answer.' The post gets 400 comments in two hours. Marketing wants to delete comments and answer 'everything is fine.'

options.t: No deleting. I'd call the client now, find the facts, and publish a short public reply: 'We're sorry. We are calling you today to fix this.' After the fix, I'd ask the client for an update. In parallel, I'd write to all active clients, so they hear it from us first.
options.c: Публичное признание, звонок клиенту, письмо активным клиентам: управление кризисом.

options.t: Delete the comments and answer 'everything is fine.' We can't allow this.
options.c: Удаление усиливает реакцию.

options.t: Ignore the post. It will go away in a day.
options.c: Молчание выглядит как согласие.

options.t: Answer in the comments that the client is wrong and show the contract.
options.c: Спор с клиентом публично ухудшает положение.

words.ex: Crisis communication needs speed and honesty.

words.how: Ответ на сообщение в открытом доступе.

steps.msg: A former client threatens to sue Atlas for 400,000, claiming a failed project. Ava asks you to prepare for a meeting with lawyers. You know the project had problems on both sides.

options.t: I'll prepare three folders: the contract and changes, the timeline with decisions, and an honest list of our mistakes. The lawyers should see the weak points first. I'd also suggest a settlement meeting before court.
options.c: Полная картина и вариант урегулирования.

options.t: I'll give the lawyers the contract and the main emails, and they will decide what is important. They know the law better.
options.c: Отдаёт без оценки.

options.t: I'll prepare the documents that show that the client was responsible for the delays, to help our defense.
options.c: Только удобные факты.

options.t: I'd prefer not to be involved. This is a legal question, and I don't want to say something that may be used against us. The client's lawyers read every email carefully. I'd pass the question to the legal team and wait.
options.c: Отстраняется.

words.how: Не удалять письма и файлы по делу.

steps.msg: The lawyers say a settlement is possible for about 120,000, but this would be seen as an admission. Ava asks: "Do we pay, or do we fight?"

options.t: I'd recommend settling for a lower number, with no admission of fault in the text, and a clear agreement about client data and references. A trial costs about 80,000 in fees, plus a risk of losing 400,000 and a damaged reputation. I'd ask the board to approve.
options.c: Взвешивает цену и риск.

options.t: I'd fight. We did not do anything wrong, and if we pay, other clients will try the same.
options.c: Принципиальность.

options.t: I'd pay the 120,000 to end the story quickly. We can't afford a long case and the stress for the team. It's not much money for a company of our size. A long case makes bad news in the press. I'd sign the paper this week.
options.c: Платит не торгуясь.

options.t: I'd wait and see what the client does next. Maybe they will not go to court, and we avoid the cost.
options.c: Ждёт.

words.how: Формулировка, что выплата не означает признания вины.
words.ex: We sign without admission of liability.

steps.msg: You are promoted to CEO. In your first all-hands, an employee asks: "You started as a coordinator here. What will be different now?" The team looks at you.

options.t: I remember what it feels like to wait for an answer for a week. So: faster decisions, honest numbers every month, and a rule that every idea gets a reply within five days. Ask me in six months how we did.
options.c: Личный опыт и три обещания.

options.t: A lot will stay the same. I believe in the strong team we have, and I'll work to make Atlas a great place for everyone.
options.c: Общие слова.

options.t: I will make some big changes. I have many ideas for the company, and you will hear about them in the next weeks. The first one will be next month. I'd not like to say more before I talk to the board.
options.c: Обещает перемены без смысла.

options.t: Not much will be different. I'm still the same person, and I hope we continue as before.
options.c: Нет посыла.

words.ex: Response time for ideas is five days.

steps.msg: After the meeting a young coordinator says: "I want to be a PM like you, but I'm afraid I'm not good enough." What do you say?

options.t: I felt the same. What helped me was asking for small projects and a mentor. I'd like to be that mentor for you, if you want. Let's meet next week and pick one project to own.
options.c: Личная история и конкретное предложение.

options.t: You will be a great PM if you work hard. Believe in yourself, and don't be afraid to ask for help.
options.c: Поддержка общими словами.

options.t: Talk to your manager about a development plan. It's their job to help you, and HR has programs. I have six people in my team and not much time. You can also find good books about career growth.
options.c: Перенаправляет.

options.t: Everyone feels like this. It's normal, and it will pass with experience, so don't worry too much.
options.c: Обесценивает.

words.ex: I want to be your mentor.

words.how: Чувство, что вы недостаточно хороши, несмотря на успехи.

steps.msg: At 7 a.m., you learn that the agency's biggest client, 35% of revenue, wants to leave in 30 days. The same morning, a rumor appears online that Atlas has financial problems. Richard calls you. What do you do first?

options.t: I'd tell Richard the facts: the client wants to leave, the reason is unclear, I'll meet them today. I'd ask for 24 hours before any public step, and call the CEO of the client personally. Then I'd tell the leadership team before they hear it from others.
options.c: Факты, звонок клиенту и своя команда первой.
options.r: Richard feels the situation is under control, and the leadership team hears it from you first.

options.t: I'd focus on the client and call them first. The rumor will fade when the client stays, and I'd tell the team later.
options.c: Теряет команду.
options.r: The team feels left out, and rumors grow faster than the facts.

options.t: I'd call a team meeting and tell everyone that the company is fine and the rumor is wrong. We need to calm the people. People like clear words. I'd say it in five minutes and leave time for questions. I'd not mention the numbers.
options.c: Говорит «всё хорошо» без данных.
options.r: The team hears a promise that proves empty within a week.

options.t: I'd ask marketing to publish a statement that the rumor is false. We should react immediately in public.
options.c: Публичная реакция без фактов.
options.r: The public statement draws more attention, and journalists call.

steps.explain: Когда уходит главный клиент, сначала соберите факты, свяжитесь с клиентом и сообщите руководству. Заявления без фактов вредят.

steps.msg: The client's CEO says: "We are not unhappy with quality. We were bought by a large group that has its own agency. We must move in 30 days." Nothing to do with Atlas performance. How do you respond?

options.t: Thank you for telling me directly. I understand the situation. Can we plan a good handover, and talk about work that may stay: the maintenance and two projects not covered by the group's agency? I'd also ask to be a reference.
options.c: Принимает, ищет остаток и репутацию.
options.r: The client's CEO thanks you, and a plan for the maintenance work is agreed.

options.t: I understand, but we have a contract with a notice period of six months. I'd remind you that we expect you to keep it. It is also a matter of fairness to the others. We have already started to plan the work without you.
options.c: Давит контрактом.
options.r: The client says the contract will not stop the group's decision, and the talk turns cold.

options.t: I'm sorry to hear that. Perhaps we can offer a discount to keep you. I'm sure the new owner will see the value of our work.
options.c: Предлагает скидку без причины.
options.r: The client says discounts are not the problem, and you lose credibility.

options.t: That's very disappointing. We have worked together for six years, and I hope you will reconsider.
options.c: Эмоции.
options.r: The client hears only emotion and ends the call quickly.

steps.explain: Если причина ухода не в качестве, согласуйте спокойный переход, ищите остающуюся работу и сохраните отношения. Давление договором не помогает.

words.how: Задачи, которые могут остаться у агентства.
words.ex: There is residual work in maintenance.

steps.msg: You must decide how to lead through the loss of 35% revenue. The team has 70 people, and you can survive for eight months without new work. Richard asks for a plan in one week.

options.t: A 90-day plan: freeze hiring, cut external costs by 15%, redeploy people to two internal products and pitch five new clients with a clear target. I'd tell the whole team the numbers, and the layoff rule: if needed, not before month four, and with notice.
options.c: План на 90 дней и открытость с командой.
options.r: The team hears the numbers, and many offer ideas to save cost.

options.t: I'd start layoffs now, 15 people, to protect the cash. A quick decision gives the best chance for the others. Fifteen people are about 12% of the company. The others will be worried for some days. I'd tell them on Friday afternoon.
options.c: Режет сразу.
options.r: Fifteen people leave and the others feel unsafe, so more resign.

options.t: I'd keep the numbers private for now. If I tell people, they will panic and the best may leave before we have a plan.
options.c: Скрывает от команды.
options.r: The team finds out the numbers from the market, and trust drops.

options.t: I'd ask the board to put in more money so that we have time. Our team is strong, and we only need a little time.
options.c: Ждёт денег.
options.r: The board asks for a plan first, and weeks pass with no action.

steps.explain: При потере крупного клиента составьте план на 90 дней и откройтесь команде о цифрах и правилах. Секретность и быстрые сокращения хуже.

words.how: Сколько месяцев компания проживёт без нового дохода.

steps.msg: Three months later two new clients signed, and the cash is stable. A journalist asks to interview you about "the agency that almost collapsed." How do you answer?

options.t: I'd say: we lost a big client, we shared the numbers with the team, and we acted fast. We are not out of danger yet, but we are in a better place. I'd thank the team by name and say what we learned about relying on one client.
options.c: Честно, благодарность команде и урок.
options.r: The article is honest, and two new clients mention it as a reason to call.

options.t: I'd say that the agency is strong, and we are growing again. It was a temporary problem, and everything is fine now.
options.c: Приукрашивает.
options.r: The article sounds good, but a former employee says the opposite.

options.t: I'd decline the interview. We don't want to talk about the problems, and it may harm new clients' trust. A reporter may ask difficult questions on live air. Our new client list is small, and one wrong sentence can cost a project.
options.c: Избегает истории.
options.r: The story is written without you, and it is less kind.

options.t: I'd blame the market and the client group for the situation. It was not our fault, and the public should know.
options.c: Перекладывает вину.
options.r: The article makes you look defensive, and the group's agency answers sharply.

steps.explain: В публичных ответах признавайте реальность, благодарите команду и показывайте урок. Приукрашивание и обвинения подрывают доверие.

endings.good: The agency passes the crisis stronger. Clients, the board and the team all see a leader who is honest and calm.
endings.mid: The agency survives, but it loses two clients and some people. The next year is about recovery.
endings.bad: The crisis damages the company deeply. You lose important people and trust, and the board changes the plan.

steps.msg: A big client asks Atlas to remove negative reviews of their product from the case study you built for them, and to write fake positive reviews for the app store. They offer a 100,000 contract. Ava is out, and you decide.

options.t: I'd decline the fake reviews clearly and politely: "We can't write fake reviews. It's against the law in many markets and against our values. But here is what we can do: a plan to collect real reviews, and fix the issues users mention."
options.c: Чёткий отказ и альтернатива.
options.r: The client listens, and the next call is about a legal way to collect reviews.

options.t: I'd say we need time to check the legal side, and I'd ask the lawyers. If it is legal, we can do it for a larger fee.
options.c: Допускает, если легально.
options.r: The lawyers say no, and the client goes to the competitor at the end of the week.

options.t: I'd say we can't help with this request and end the call. The client should find another agency for it. We have no free people now. The client's budget is also very small. I'd not suggest another agency by name.
options.c: Отказывается без альтернативы.
options.r: The client leaves, and you do not explain the reason to the team.

options.t: I'd agree. The contract is large, and many companies do this. It's a common practice in the industry.
options.c: Принимает неэтичное.
options.r: The reviews go live, and a journalist discovers them in a month.

steps.explain: Отказывайтесь от неэтичных просьб ясно и вежливо, объясняйте причину и предлагайте законную альтернативу.

words.how: Придуманные отзывы от людей, которых нет.
Следование принципам, даже когда это дорого.
words.ex: Integrity matters more than one contract.
We decline politely and offer an alternative.

steps.msg: The client answers: "Your competitor said yes without a problem. If you don't help, I'll give them the whole contract, including the real work." The pressure is high.

options.t: I understand the pressure. I'd hold the line: we do the real work well, and we don't do the reviews. If the contract goes to the competitor, we accept the loss. I'd ask for a 30-minute call to show our plan for real reviews.
options.c: Держит границу, открыт к разговору.
options.r: The client hears the plan and, after some days, asks for a proposal on real reviews.

options.t: I'd ask for time and promise a decision tomorrow. Then I'd ask Ava, because it is a big money question. The sum is very high for me. Ava has done similar deals before. I'd call her in the next hour.
options.c: Откладывает ответ.
options.r: The client waits one day, and your answer is the same, which is now more tense.

options.t: Okay, let's do a milder version: we write positive reviews but without false facts. It's a compromise.
options.c: Компромисс всё равно обман.
options.r: The client says a half version is still fake, and ends the call.

options.t: Let me think about it. I'd say yes without telling the team, and I'd manage the details myself.
options.c: Скрытно соглашается.
options.r: The client talks to your team behind your back, and you lose control.

steps.explain: Под давлением конкурентов держите границу и предлагайте законный путь. Скрытые договорённости и «мягкие» версии обмана остаются обманом.

words.ex: The client gives us an ultimatum.
Fake reviews are a reputational risk.

steps.msg: A week later you learn that a team member wrote five positive reviews for the client on his own, because he did not want to lose the contract. He did not tell anyone. He asks for your support.

options.t: I'd ask him to remove them today, and thank him for telling me. We'd talk about it: why he did it, and what he needs to feel safe to say no. Then I'd tell the leadership team about the case and the rule, without punishing him unfairly.
options.c: Исправление, разговор и правило.
options.r: The employee removes the reviews, and the team sees that mistakes can be handled calmly.

options.t: I'd ask him to remove the reviews and not to do it again. I'd keep the case between us, so that he doesn't have problems.
options.c: Скрывает случай от руководства.
options.r: The leadership team learns of the case from the client a month later.

options.t: I'd fire him. It's a serious violation of our values, and the rest of the team must see the consequences.
options.c: Жёстко без разговора.
options.r: The team becomes afraid, and people hide mistakes more often.

options.t: I'd leave the reviews, since it's done, and the client is happy. It's too late to change it, and there is no need to make a drama. It would cost two days of work for the editor. The client has not noticed the problem.
options.c: Позволяет нарушение.
options.r: The reviews stay online, and the client later uses them in an ad.

steps.explain: Исправьте нарушение сразу, поговорите с человеком и сообщите руководству. Скрытие и жёсткое наказание без разговора одинаково слабы.

words.how: Атмосфера, где можно говорить о проблемах.

endings.good: You protect your values and the relationship. The client respects you, and the team sees where the line is.
endings.mid: You keep the client but lose some trust inside the team. You know you must set clearer rules for the next case.
endings.bad: You lose both the client and the team's respect. You remember this case as a turning point.

tone.ctx: A team member replies to the minutes: 'That's not what I agreed to. I never said I'd do the integration.' Write your reply.

opts.t: Thanks for checking. My notes say you took the integration, but let's confirm it now. Could you tell me what you understood, so I can correct the minutes if needed?
opts.c: Не обвиняет, сверяет понимание и обещает поправить протокол при необходимости.

opts.t: It's in the minutes. You said it in the meeting.
opts.c: Тон обвинения: человек замкнётся, а недопонимание останется.

opts.t: Oh, sorry, I probably wrote it wrong, I'll delete it, no problem.
opts.c: Мгновенная уступка: поручение исчезает, и никто его не делает.

b01.build: could you tell me what you understood so i can correct the minutes

tone.ctx: Mia answers: 'I have three other clients today. Why is this always urgent?' Write your reply.

opts.t: I understand you're busy, and I'm sorry this feels urgent. The developers are waiting for exactly this file. Which part could you send first, even in draft?
opts.c: Признаёт загрузку и предлагает компромисс: сначала часть, даже черновик.

opts.t: Your other clients are not my problem. We have a deadline.
opts.c: Пренебрежительно: Миа почувствует, что её время не ценят.

opts.t: Oh, sorry, then forget it, I'll tell the developers to wait as long as needed.
opts.c: Полная уступка: проект остановится, а срок уйдёт.

b02.build: which part could you send first even if it is only a draft

tone.ctx: Chloe replies: 'This is the second time a date has moved. I'm losing trust.' Write your reply.

opts.t: You're right, and I understand. To rebuild trust, I'll send you a short status every Monday and Thursday, and I'll tell you the same day if any date is at risk.
opts.c: Признаёт проблему и вводит конкретный ритм коммуникации.

opts.t: Both delays were small, and nothing is at risk. Please be patient.
opts.c: Обесценивает чувства клиента вместо действий.

opts.t: I'm very sorry, it's all my fault, I promise it won't happen again, I swear.
opts.c: Клятвы без механизма: через неделю доверие рухнет снова.

b03.build: i will tell you the same day if any date is at risk

tone.ctx: Julia calls Chloe, who says: 'I saw the discount idea. So you can give me a discount?' Julia asks you to write a short note for Chloe. Write it.

opts.t: Chloe, you received an internal email by mistake, and we apologize. Please delete it. Any pricing change goes through Julia and the contract, so let's talk about your budget openly on Thursday.
opts.c: Извиняется, просит удалить и переводит разговор в законное русло.

opts.t: That email was not meant for you. Please delete it and don't mention it.
opts.c: Требование молчать выглядит как скрытие и вызывает недоверие.

opts.t: Sorry, maybe a small discount is possible, I don't know, I'd have to ask.
opts.c: Намёк на скидку подрывает позицию Джулии на переговорах.

b04.build: any pricing change goes through julia and the contract
