options.t: In the first month, I write the requirements document. It's the main output of the job, and everybody waits for it. I'd also draw a diagram. The team will read it in the first week. Max can review it on Friday.
options.c: Только документ.

options.t: I attend all meetings, take notes and learn how the project works. After that, I start to work. A new analyst learns a lot by listening. The senior people can lead the work in the first month. It is not my place to propose.
options.c: Пассивно.

options.t: I do what the product owner asks me. The analyst helps the team by following instructions.
options.c: Исполнитель.

steps.msg: The candidate asks: "How do you handle a stakeholder who changes his mind every week?" You have met such a person.

options.t: I try to find out why he changes it. Often the goal is not clear, or he gets new information. I'd write a short summary after every meeting, ask him to confirm, and show the cost of each change. That helps both sides.
options.c: Причина, подтверждение и цена.

options.t: I'd say that I follow his latest decision, and I tell the team about each change so that they are ready.
options.c: Подстраивается.

options.t: I'd ask my manager to talk to him. A stakeholder like this needs a senior person to manage him. He is hard to talk to. My manager has more weight. I'd stay out of the meetings with him.
options.c: Эскалирует.

options.t: I'd stop to work with him until he decides what he wants. It is not possible to work in such a way.
options.c: Отказывается.

words.ex: The goal is a moving target.

steps.msg: Alex says: "Your requirements are ready, but I need a short handover so that my testers understand the main flows." You have one hour tomorrow.

options.t: I'd do a 45-minute session: 10 minutes on the goal, 20 minutes on the main flows with a diagram, 10 minutes on the risky cases, and 5 minutes for questions. I'd send the diagram and a short list in advance.
options.c: План сессии и материалы заранее.

options.t: I'd go through the document page by page, and the testers can ask questions during the session. The testers will read the parts they need. A few questions after each page keep everybody awake. It takes about two hours. The first page has the main part.
options.c: Читает документ.

options.t: I'd send the document and tell the testers to write to me if they have any questions. Alex's team is experienced. A long handover takes an hour from everyone. The document explains the flows.
options.c: Отправляет файл.

options.t: I'd say that the requirements are clear, and a handover is not needed. Testers can read them.
options.c: Отказывается.

words.how: Показ сценария от начала до конца.
words.ex: Give a walkthrough of the main flow.

steps.msg: During the handover, a tester asks: "What happens when the customer's card is blocked in the middle of a transfer?" You do not know.

options.t: I don't know yet, and it is an important case. I'll check with Nina and Olga today and add it to the requirements and your test list by tomorrow noon. Thank you for asking.
options.c: Честно, срок и обновление.

options.t: I think that the transfer should stop. I'll add this to the requirements, and I'll check it later with Nina.
options.c: Предполагает.

options.t: That is a rare case. I'd not worry about it now, and we can look at it after the release. Nobody knows how often it happens. The release is on Friday. A rare case can wait.
options.c: Откладывает.

options.t: It is a technical question for the developers. Please ask Nina during the testing.
options.c: Перекидывает.

words.ex: I will follow up by noon.

steps.msg: In the sprint review, Greg, the CIO, says: "This is good, but customers also need a calendar view, a spending chart and the export to Excel." Helen nods and says: "Yes, let's add them." You look at the team and see tired faces.

options.t: Thank you, these are strong ideas. Before we decide, I'd like to see what each one costs and what it brings. I'll prepare a table by Thursday with the effort, the value and the effect on the date. Then you and Helen choose.
options.c: Не отказывает, просит данные.
options.r: Greg and Helen wait for the table, and the room calms down.

options.t: These are good ideas. I'd add them to the backlog, and we will look at them after the release.
options.c: Откладывает без анализа.
options.r: The ideas are saved, but Greg feels that nobody took them seriously.

options.t: I think we can add the three features, but the date will move. I'd tell the team to work with the new plan and decide about the new date later. I'd tell Helen after the planning. The team needs a few days to react.
options.c: Принимает и сдвигает.
options.r: The team hears about extra work without a date, and morale falls.

options.t: I don't think we can do this. The team is tired, and the scope is already big. I'd say it clearly, so we don't lose time.
options.c: Резко отказывает.
options.r: Greg feels rejected in front of Helen, and the talk becomes tense.

steps.explain: Когда руководитель просит добавить функции при готовом объёме, не соглашайтесь сразу и не отказывайте резко. Предложите таблицу стоимости, пользы и влияния на срок.

words.ex: The sprint review is on Friday.

steps.msg: Your table shows: the calendar view costs 3 weeks and has medium value, the spending chart costs 2 weeks and has high value, and the export costs 1 week and has low value. The date is in 5 weeks, and the base scope needs 4 weeks.

options.t: The base scope needs four of the five weeks. The spending chart has the highest value for its cost, but it needs two weeks, so the date moves by one week. I'd recommend adding only the chart and moving the date by one week, and putting the others in the next release.
options.c: Рекомендация с цифрами.
options.r: Greg and Helen choose the chart with a one-week delay, and the team agrees.

options.t: I'd add the export and the chart. They need three weeks together, and the date moves by two weeks. Both are not too hard. The export is a small part of the work. The chart has a high value. The delay of two weeks is acceptable.
options.c: Берёт две.
options.r: The team gets three weeks of extra work, and the date moves by two weeks.

options.t: I'd show the table and ask Greg and Helen to choose. It is their decision, and I'd follow it.
options.c: Нет рекомендации.
options.r: Greg and Helen choose by feeling, and no one owns the effect on the date.

options.t: I'd add all three features and ask the team to work faster, because the executives want them. The chart and the calendar view are not so big. The weekend work is only for two weeks. I'd thank the team at the party. The team likes to be asked for a big effort.
options.c: Всё сразу.
options.r: The team gets too much work, and quality falls.

steps.explain: Показывайте варианты с цифрами и давайте рекомендацию. Лучше добавить одну ценную функцию, чем все три.

words.ex: The base scope needs four weeks.
We have one week of buffer.

steps.msg: Greg agrees to the chart, but says: "And please don't change the date. I promised it to the board." Tom says: "We can't do both without working weekends."

options.t: I understand the promise to the board. Here are three options: keep the date and do the base scope only, move the date by one week with the chart, or keep the date with the chart and reduce the test time, which raises the risk of bugs. I recommend the second option, and I'd explain the reason to the board.
options.c: Три варианта, честная рекомендация.
options.r: Greg accepts one extra week, and Tom's team keeps the full test time.

options.t: I'd keep the date and add the chart, but we reduce the testing. I'd monitor the risk closely, and we'll fix bugs after the release.
options.c: Уступает ради срока.
options.r: The release is on time, but a bug appears in the first week.

options.t: I'd ask the team to work on weekends for two weekends, and I'd thank them in front of the executives.
options.c: Давит на людей.
options.r: Two weekends pass, and two people say they are close to burnout.

options.t: I'd say that we will do our best to keep the date and add the chart. We'll see what happens. The team has a good record. Helen likes optimism. A date can be changed in the last week. Ask Sam to confirm the date every week.
options.c: Неопределённость.
options.r: Greg waits for the plan, and the date stays unclear for another week.

steps.explain: Если сроки и рамки конфликтуют, назовите варианты и последствия каждого. Не жертвуйте качеством и людьми, чтобы не сказать «нет».

words.ex: The date is a commitment to the board.

steps.msg: After the release, Helen asks: "How can we avoid this uncontrolled growth in the future?" She wants a simple method.

options.t: Three rules: every new request goes into a short form with its goal, cost and value. A weekly 15-minute meeting decides what to accept. And the date moves only with a written decision by Helen and Greg. I'd start next sprint.
options.c: Простая процедура изменений.
options.r: Helen and Greg sign a simple rule, and the next sprint goes smoothly.

options.t: I'd ask everyone to send new ideas through me, and I'd decide what to add and what to leave for later. It is easier for the team when one person decides. The list will grow every week. I'd review it on Mondays.
options.c: Решает сам.
options.r: Requests start to wait for you, and the team feels slow.

options.t: I'd make a long, detailed procedure for changes, with several approval levels. It would give us full control.
options.c: Слишком тяжело.
options.r: Nobody uses the long procedure, and changes happen outside it.

options.t: I think we should avoid such situations by saying no more often. Then the scope will stay small.
options.c: Просто «нет».
options.r: New requests keep coming, and the same problem repeats.

steps.explain: Для контроля объёма нужна простая процедура: форма запроса, регулярная встреча и письменное решение об изменении срока.

words.how: Порядок подачи и оценки новых запросов.

endings.good: You kept the project in control, and every change had a clear price. Helen and the team trust your numbers, and the release is on time.
endings.mid: The release is late by a few weeks, and some stakeholders feel their requests were ignored.
endings.bad: The scope keeps growing, the team burns out, and the project is stopped and restarted with new rules.

steps.msg: Customers wait 12 days for a card reissue, but the target is 5. Support says the delay is in operations, operations say it is in logistics, and logistics say it is the bank's printing partner. Rita asks you to "find out where the problem is."

options.t: I'd map the process from the customer's request to the card in the hand, and take timestamps from the systems for each step. Then we'll see where the days go, based on facts. I'd come back with the map in three days.
options.c: Карта процесса с данными.
options.r: You get a clear map with days per step, and the teams see the same picture.

options.t: I'd talk to each team and ask them to explain their step. Then I'd decide where the delay is.
options.c: Опирается на рассказы.
options.r: Each team defends itself, and the picture stays unclear.

options.t: I'd focus on the printing partner, because outside companies are usually the cause of delays. The logs show many delays at the partner. A phone call to them is a quick step. Rita has the contact.
options.c: Угадывает.
options.r: The partner is checked, but it is not the cause, and time is lost.

options.t: I'd send a message to all three teams asking them to work faster and improve their steps.
options.c: Общий призыв.
options.r: The teams agree to improve, but nothing changes in practice.

steps.explain: Если команды обвиняют друг друга, постройте карту процесса с временными метками. Решения принимайте по фактам.

words.how: Сколько длится процесс от начала до конца.

words.ex: The service level is five days.

steps.msg: The map shows: 1 day in support, 3 days in operations, 7 days waiting in logistics, because nobody is responsible for sending the batch of cards. Each team thinks that another team does it.

options.t: The largest delay is seven days in logistics, and it is a handover gap: no one owns the batch sending. I'd propose to Rita that one person owns the whole process from request to delivery, and I'd show the map to all three teams in one meeting.
options.c: Находит разрыв и владельца.
options.r: Rita names an owner, and the teams meet to fix the handover.

options.t: I'd ask logistics to start sending the cards every day, and the problem will go away. A daily batch is easy to start. Logistics already has a van every morning. We don't need new tools. It saves a lot of time on both sides.
options.c: Закрывает симптом.
options.r: Cards leave logistics daily, but the next gap appears elsewhere.

options.t: I'd tell the teams that the delay is mainly on the logistics side, and I'd suggest they improve their work.
options.c: Обвиняет.
options.r: Logistics feels blamed and slows down its cooperation.

options.t: I'd send the map to Rita and let her decide who is responsible. It is a management question.
options.c: Отходит.
options.r: Rita waits for you to propose, and the problem stays for another month.

steps.explain: Задержки часто возникают на стыке команд, где нет владельца. Назначьте одного ответственного за процесс от начала до конца.

steps.msg: Rita agrees to name a process owner. A month later, the delay is 6 days. Rita asks: "How do we make sure it stays this way?"

options.t: I'd add a simple dashboard with the average days per step, with a weekly review by the process owner and an alert if the total is over 7 days. I'd also write the one-page process with the owner's name on it.
options.c: Метрика, обзор, оповещение.
options.r: The dashboard shows each step, and the owner reacts in the first week.

options.t: I'd ask the process owner to check the status every week and tell us if something goes wrong. One check a week is enough. The owner has the data. Rita will be happy with a short mail.
options.c: Без измерений.
options.r: The owner checks the status, but he cannot see small delays early.

options.t: I'd write a long process document, so that everyone knows the rules and can follow them.
options.c: Документ.
options.r: The document is long, and few people read it.

options.t: I think the process is fine now. We should wait and see if a new problem appears. The delay in cards is not visible anymore. A new report will show the answer in a month. The owner is in place, and that is enough.
options.c: Ждёт.
options.r: Three months later, the delay returns without anyone noticing.

steps.explain: Чтобы улучшение сохранилось, нужны метрика, регулярный обзор и порог для оповещения.

words.how: Значение, при превышении которого нужно действовать.
words.ex: The alert threshold is seven days.

endings.good: You found the real owner, fixed the process and made a clear rule. Teams cooperate, and the work is faster.
endings.mid: The immediate problem is fixed, but the owner question stays open, and similar issues will appear again.
endings.bad: Teams blame each other, the process gets worse, and customers wait longer.

steps.msg: You write an API specification with Nina for a new endpoint that returns the customer's loan balance. Nina asks: 'What should the endpoint return if the customer has no loans?'

options.t: Good question. I'd suggest an empty list and a normal success response, not an error, because having no loans is not a failure. I'll confirm it with Helen and document the response codes: 200 with an empty list, 401 for no access, 404 only if the customer does not exist.
options.c: Пустой список и успешный ответ: «нет кредитов» — не ошибка; коды ответа описаны.

options.t: I'd return an error, so the app knows there are no loans.
options.c: Ошибка для нормального состояния усложнит приложение.

options.t: I'd return a null value. It's the simplest.
options.c: Null путает пустое значение и отсутствие данных.

options.t: It's up to the developers. They know best.
options.c: Контракт интерфейса — совместное решение.

words.how: Адрес, по которому клиент получает данные.
words.ex: The endpoint returns the loan balance.

steps.msg: Helen asks for a change: 'Let's add a new loan type, student loan, with its own rules.' Tom says: 'I need to know what else will change.' You must do an impact analysis.

options.t: I'd check four areas: screens, rules and calculations, integrations with other systems, and reports. For each I'd list what changes, who owns it, and the effort. I'll also mark risks and unknowns. I can bring the first version in two days, for Tom and Helen to review.
options.c: Четыре области, владельцы, трудозатраты, риски и срок.

options.t: I'd ask Tom what will change. He knows the system.
options.c: Тон не знает бизнес-правил и отчётности.

options.t: I'd say it's a small change. We already have other loan types.
options.c: «Небольшое» без анализа — риск пропущенных связей.

options.t: I'd start the work and see what breaks.
options.c: Попытка вслепую: цена ошибок высока.

words.how: Формула для суммы, процента или платежа.
words.ex: The calculation changes for student loans.

steps.msg: Rita often rejects your proposals with 'this will not work in real life' and gives no details. In today's meeting she does it again. You have two minutes left.

options.t: Rita, I want this to work in real life, and you know it better than I do. Could you tell me which step will fail and why? I'd like to visit your team on Thursday to see it, and then I'll change the proposal. Could we also try it with one team as a pilot?
options.c: Признаёт её опыт, просит конкретный шаг, предлагает визит и пилот.

options.t: Rita, you always say that. Please give me specific reasons.
options.c: Упрёк закрывает разговор.

options.t: Okay, let's skip this proposal. It's not going to work.
options.c: Отказ от предложения без попытки понять причину.

options.t: I'll go to Greg and tell him that Rita blocks the project.
options.c: Эскалация перед разговором разрушает отношения.

words.ex: Expect pushback on the new process.
Ask about the concern behind the objection.
Run a pilot with one team.

steps.msg: You map customer data from the old core banking system to the new one. In the old system, the field 'status' has 12 values. In the new system, it has 5. Leo asks how you will handle it.

options.t: I'd list all 12 old values with the number of customers for each, then propose a mapping to the 5 new values. For values with no clear match, I'd ask Olga and Rita what they mean in practice. I'd record the mapping rules and test them on a sample before the migration.
options.c: Список значений с количеством клиентов, правила маппинга, консультации и тест на выборке.

options.t: I'll map the 12 values to the closest of the 5. It's the easiest.
options.c: «Ближайшее» значение может поменять смысл статуса.

options.t: I'll ask the developers to create 12 values in the new system.
options.c: Изменение целевой модели без анализа.

options.t: I'll ignore the values that have only a few customers.
options.c: Редкие значения могут быть самыми рискованными.

words.how: Правила перевода значений из старой системы в новую.

words.ex: The migration runs on the weekend.

words.how: Значение, существующее только в старой системе.

steps.msg: Nina says: 'If the app sends the same payment twice because of a bad network, we may charge the customer twice. We need to handle it.' You write the requirement.

options.t: 'Each payment request has a unique key from the app. If the system gets the same key again, it returns the first result and does not charge again.' I'd add a test case: send the same request twice, and check one charge. And I'd set how long keys are stored, such as 24 hours.
options.c: Уникальный ключ, повторный ответ без списания, тест и срок хранения ключей.

options.t: 'The system must not charge the customer twice.'
options.c: Нельзя проверить: нет механизма.

options.t: 'The app should send the payment only once.'
options.c: Приложение не может гарантировать единичность при сбое сети.

options.t: 'The system should detect duplicate payments, if possible.'
options.c: «Если возможно» — не требование.

words.how: Повторный запрос даёт тот же результат без побочных эффектов.

words.ex: Send a unique key with each request.

steps.msg: Zoe sends you her requirements document for review. It has many mistakes: unclear words, missing cases and long sentences. She is new and is proud of her work.

options.t: Thank you for sending it, Zoe. The structure is good. I have three comments: define unclear words like 'quickly,' add the case of an empty list, and cut long sentences into two. Let's go through the first page together, and then you can do the rest. I'm glad to review it again.
options.c: Сначала сильное, затем три приоритетных замечания и совместный разбор первой страницы.

options.t: There are many mistakes. You need to rewrite the whole document.
options.c: Полная переработка без приоритетов демотивирует.

options.t: I'll fix it myself and send it back. It's faster.
options.c: Исправление за неё не учит.

options.t: It's good. Just a few small things, and you can send it.
options.c: Скрывает проблемы: документ пойдёт дальше с ошибками.

steps.msg: Greg asks you to prepare a short business case for automating the loan document check. Today 12 operators spend 40% of their time on it. A tool costs $200,000 a year.

options.t: I'd show the cost today: 12 operators at 40% is about five full-time people. I'd add the cost of the tool and the setup, the expected saving, the risks like errors in recognition, and the payback time. I'd offer two scenarios, conservative and expected, and a recommendation. One page, with a detailed table behind it.
options.c: Затраты сегодня, стоимость инструмента, экономия, риски, срок окупаемости, два сценария и рекомендация.

options.t: I'd say that automation saves 100% of the time. It's a great investment.
options.c: Автоматизация не убирает 100% времени.

options.t: I'd show only the benefits. The costs make the case weaker.
options.c: Скрытие затрат разрушит доверие.

options.t: I'd copy a business case from another project and change the numbers.
options.c: Копирование чужих данных нарушает смысл кейса.

words.how: Документ с затратами, выгодами и рисками.

steps.msg: An audit finds that your loan approval process has no record of who approved exceptions. Olga says: 'We need a fix in four weeks, and we need evidence.' You must write the requirement.

options.t: I'd write a requirement: each exception must be saved with the approver's name, the date, the reason and the amount. I'd add a report for audit, agree on the retention period with Olga, and a test that proves it works. By week four I'd have a screenshot-based evidence pack for the auditor.
options.c: Поля записи, отчёт для аудита, срок хранения, тест и пакет доказательств.

options.t: I'd write: 'The system must keep a record of exceptions.'
options.c: Не определено, что записывать и как проверить.

options.t: I'd ask the operators to write exceptions in a spreadsheet.
options.c: Таблица не защищена и не встроена в процесс.

options.t: I'd ask the auditor to give us more time.
options.c: Просьба о времени без плана.

words.ex: The system must keep an audit trail.

steps.msg: You find that Rita's team uses a private Excel file to track urgent loan cases, because the system does not support it. The file has customer data on a shared drive that anyone can open.

options.t: Thank you for showing me. The file solves a real problem, so I want to build it into the system. In the meantime, I'd ask to keep it in a protected folder with limited access, and I'll tell Olga, so nobody is surprised. Could we write down what the file does, so I can make a requirement?
options.c: Признаёт ценность файла, защищает данные временно, уведомляет комплаенс и собирает требование.

options.t: Customer data in a spreadsheet is not allowed. Please delete it today.
options.c: Удаление без замены разрушит работу.

options.t: I'll ignore it. It's their business.
options.c: Игнорирование оставляет риск утечки.

options.t: I'll report it to compliance right away. It's a violation.
options.c: Немедленный донос без разговора разрушит доверие.

words.ex: The Excel file is a workaround.

words.how: Инструменты, которыми пользуются без одобрения ИТ.
Кто может открыть и изменить данные.
words.ex: Add access control to the folder.

steps.msg: At 2 p.m. the day after a release, the support team sees a rise in failed payments, from 1% to 6%. Tom asks: 'Should we roll back or fix forward?' You are the analyst on duty.

options.t: I'd check two things in 15 minutes: which customers fail, and whether the cause is the form or the fee. If we cannot find the cause in 30 minutes, I'd recommend rolling back, because the failure rate is high and customers lose money. I'll stay on the call and keep the log of facts.
options.c: Короткая диагностика, срок принятия решения и протокол фактов.

options.t: Let's fix forward. Rolling back is always embarrassing.
options.c: Стыд не критерий решения.

options.t: Let's roll back right now. It's the safest.
options.c: Откат без диагностики может потерять исправления.

options.t: Let's wait and see if the failure rate changes.
options.c: Ожидание при 6% отказов дорого стоит.

words.how: Исправить дефект в новой версии без отката.
words.ex: We fix forward with a patch.

steps.msg: Marcus, the CEO, says: "I want a chatbot that approves loans in five minutes. The competitor has one. Can we launch in two months?" You know that the scoring and the data are not ready.

options.t: I like the goal. In two months we can build a chatbot that collects the application and gives a preliminary answer, but not a final decision, because the scoring and compliance checks need more time. I'd show you a plan with the final version in six months.
options.c: Часть цели сейчас, остальное по плану.

options.t: I'd say that it is a good idea, and we will do our best. I'd ask the team to start and look at the problems when they appear.
options.c: Обещает.

options.t: It is not possible in two months. The scoring is not ready, and the risk is too high. I'd propose to wait until next year.
options.c: Отказывает.

options.t: I'd say yes and plan the work. If the team cannot do it, we will explain the reasons to the CEO later. The CEO likes ambitious plans. A "no" would sound weak. The team will find a way. The team is strong and can learn quickly.
options.c: Соглашается.

steps.msg: Marcus answers: "Preliminary is not good enough. The press will say that our competitor is faster." He is not happy.

options.t: I understand. The press matters. A preliminary answer in five minutes is already fast, and we can describe it as "instant pre-approval." The final decision needs a few hours for checks, which also protects customers and the bank. I'd bring two sample messages for the press team.
options.c: Находит формулировку и объясняет причину.

options.t: I understand the pressure. I'd ask the risk team if they could accept a faster final decision for small loans. Small loans have a lower risk. The risk team likes to help. We can set a limit of $1,000. I'd send them the example in an email.
options.c: Предлагает исключение.

options.t: I'd say that I'm sorry, but we cannot change the facts. The press may say what they want.
options.c: Не помогает.

options.t: I'd ask Helen to talk to Marcus. She is better in explaining product questions to the CEO.
options.c: Передаёт.

steps.msg: Nina says: "Your specification says that the app sends the date as text, but our system uses a timestamp. We need to agree." She has already started to code with timestamps.

options.t: Thank you for telling me early. I'd suggest we use timestamps in UTC, as in your code, and I'd update the specification today. Let's also agree on the rule for time zones, and add one example to the document.
options.c: Принимает лучшее решение.

options.t: Let me check with the app team first. If they can send a timestamp, I'd agree, and I'll tell you soon.
options.c: Сначала проверит.

options.t: My specification was approved, so please follow it. It is not good to change the contract during development.
options.c: Настаивает.

options.t: I'd say that we can go on with both and decide later, if there is a problem. The two formats can live together for a while. We see which one causes fewer problems. Nobody has to change the code today.
options.c: Откладывает.

words.how: Соглашение о формате и значении данных.

words.ex: Use a timestamp for the date.

steps.msg: The next day, Nina sees that the app team sends the time in local time without a time zone. Some transfers show the wrong date for customers abroad.

options.t: This is a good example of why the rule matters. I'd ask the app team to send UTC with the zone. I'd add a test case for a customer in another time zone, and I'd check the old transfers with Alex.
options.c: Исправляет причину, тест и проверка.

options.t: I'd ask Nina to convert the time on her side, because she can do it quickly and we avoid a new release of the app. Nina's code is already close. A new app release takes two weeks. The customers will not see a difference.
options.c: Решает на стороне сервера.

options.t: I'd write a note for customers, that the date may show wrongly in some cases, and we'll fix it later.
options.c: Прячет проблему.

options.t: I'd say it is a problem of the app team, and not of the specification. They must read the document carefully.
options.c: Обвиняет.

words.ex: Convert to UTC on the server.

steps.msg: On Monday morning, support receives 140 messages from customers who were charged twice for card payments over the weekend. Helen writes: "We need to know what happened, right now. Can you lead the analysis?"

options.t: Yes. I'd start with three questions: how many customers, what amount, and since when? I'd ask Tom's team for the logs and Alex to check what changed in the release. I'd send you a first update in one hour, even if it is incomplete.
options.c: Три вопроса, команда, срок.
options.r: Helen sees a clear plan, and the first update arrives within the hour.

options.t: Yes. I'd ask Tom to find the technical cause first. When we know it, we can decide what to tell customers.
options.c: Ждёт причину.
options.r: The cause is found, but customers wait longer without any message.

options.t: Yes. I'd check the release notes from last Friday and look for the likely cause. I think it is probably related to the new payment form.
options.c: Догадывается.
options.r: The guess is partly right, and you lose time on the wrong branch of the release.

options.t: I'd wait until we have more data, because early information may be wrong and cause panic. A wrong number would harm us. The first hours are always chaotic. I'd write to Helen at noon. The count of customers is still unclear.
options.c: Ждёт данных.
options.r: The problem grows over the morning, and more customers are charged.

steps.explain: При инциденте с деньгами клиентов сразу задайте три вопроса: сколько клиентов, какая сумма и с какого времени. Дайте первый апдейт в течение часа, даже неполный.

steps.msg: The logs show: after a short network failure on Saturday at 11 p.m., the app retried the payment requests, and the server processed both. 312 customers are affected. The total is $41,000. Support asks what to tell customers.

options.t: I'd give support a short text: "We found a technical problem, you were charged twice, and we will return the money within two working days. You don't need to do anything." I'd attach the list of affected customers and ask Olga to review the text.
options.c: Короткий текст и проверка.
options.r: Support sends a clear message, and customers feel the bank takes care.

options.t: I'd tell support to say that we are working on the problem, and that customers will get information soon. The system will be back soon. The news can be short. I'd not give a time.
options.c: Расплывчато.
options.r: Customers get a vague promise and call support again.

options.t: I'd tell support not to give details, and to write to each customer separately when we have the refund ready. Each customer has a different case. A standard text sounds cold. We can send emails in two days. The list of affected customers is long.
options.c: Скрывает.
options.r: Customers write to each other about the problem before the bank speaks.

options.t: I'd say that a few customers may have a problem, and that it is under review.
options.c: Занижает масштаб.
options.r: The scale is hidden, and a journalist later finds the real number.

steps.explain: Клиентам скажите, что случилось, что вы делаете и когда вернёте деньги. Не занижайте масштаб и не молчите.

words.how: Сообщения клиентам о проблеме и решении.

words.ex: Process the refunds in two days.
The root cause is the retry.

steps.msg: Tom says: "The fix is simple: add a unique key to each payment, and the server ignores a repeated key. It takes three days." Greg asks: "Why did our tests not find it?" You wrote the payment requirements last year and did not include this case.

options.t: It is a gap in my requirements: I did not include the repeated request after a failure. I'd add it now, with the unique key rule, and write a test case for a bad network. I'd also check other payment flows for the same gap this week.
options.c: Признаёт, исправляет и проверяет остальное.
options.r: The team accepts the gap, and the fix and the check of other flows go ahead.

options.t: The test environment did not have the network problem, so it was difficult to find the case. I'd ask Alex to make the test environment more realistic. The error needs a very special network failure. Alex can write a test for it in a week. I'd ask Tom to confirm the cause.
options.c: Объясняет окружением.
options.r: Alex improves the test environment, but the missing requirement stays unknown.

options.t: This case is quite unusual, and it is difficult to predict everything. I think the team did what was reasonable. Very few teams test this case. It happened on a Saturday night. Nobody could expect it.
options.c: Оправдывается.
options.r: Greg is not satisfied, and he asks for a deeper review.

options.t: I'd say that the developers should have handled it in the code. It's a standard technical issue.
options.c: Перекладывает.
options.r: The team feels blamed, and the discussion turns into a conflict.

steps.explain: Признайте пробел в требованиях и предложите исправление и проверку похожих мест. Не объясняйте всё окружением и не перекладывайте на других.

words.how: Что система делает при сбое запроса.

steps.msg: A week later, all refunds are done. Marcus asks you for a short postmortem for the executives. He wants "what happened, why, and what changes."

options.t: I'd write one page: the timeline, the cause in simple words, how many customers and how much money, what we did, and three actions with owners and dates: the unique key, a network test, and a check of other flows. No names, no blame.
options.c: Один лист, действия с владельцами.
options.r: The executives read one page and approve three actions with owners.

options.t: I'd send a short summary with the main facts and the fix, and offer to answer questions. The summary is one page. The executives read it in three minutes. I'd attach the logs. The details are not needed for the board.
options.c: Без действий.
options.r: The executives get the facts, but they cannot see who will do what.

options.t: I'd write a detailed technical report with logs and code examples, for completeness.
options.c: Слишком технично.
options.r: The report is long, and nobody reads past the first page.

options.t: I'd say that the problem was already fixed and the customers are happy, and that a report is not needed.
options.c: Пропускает отчёт.
options.r: The executives ask questions anyway, and trust in the team falls.

steps.explain: Хороший постмортем короткий и без обвинений: что случилось, почему, сколько и какие действия с владельцами и сроками.

words.ex: Each corrective action has an owner.

endings.good: You helped the team find the cause, protect customers and fix the process. Customers get their money back, and the team learns a clear lesson.
endings.mid: The problem is fixed, but you were slow in some steps, and some customers still wait for refunds.
endings.bad: The problem grows, customers lose trust, and the bank faces complaints and a fine from the regulator.

steps.msg: Nordline replaces its core banking system. You must show the executives in one picture how 14 systems exchange data today. You have a long list of interfaces and no diagram.

options.t: I'd draw one context diagram with the systems as boxes and the data flows as arrows, with the owner of each system. I'd mark the three flows that the core replacement affects most, and use color for critical systems. The detailed interface list stays in an appendix.
options.c: Контекстная диаграмма: системы, потоки, владельцы и три затронутых потока; детали в приложении.

options.t: I'd show the full list of 14 systems and all their interfaces on one slide.
options.c: Все интерфейсы на одном слайде: нечитаемо.

options.t: I'd explain the systems one by one in words.
options.c: Словесное описание не показывает связей.

options.t: I'd ask the architect to show his technical diagram.
options.c: Техническая схема архитектора не рассчитана на руководителей.

words.how: Карта всех систем и связей между ними.
words.ex: Show the system landscape on one page.

steps.msg: Nina asks: 'Should the new core send balance updates to the app in real time, or in batches every 15 minutes?' The business says: 'Customers want to see their balance immediately.'

options.t: I'd ask what 'immediately' means for the customer. If a delay of a few seconds is fine, real time with a message queue works. I'd compare the cost and the risk of both, and test with real behavior, for example how often customers check the balance after a payment. Then we choose.
options.c: Уточняет «сразу» в цифрах, сравнивает цену и риск и опирается на поведение клиентов.

options.t: Real time is always better. Customers expect it.
options.c: Real time всегда лучше: нет, цена выше.

options.t: Batches are cheaper and simpler. Let's use them.
options.c: Пакеты могут не удовлетворить ожиданий клиентов.

options.t: Let's ask the architect to decide.
options.c: Решение требует бизнес-контекста.

words.ex: Balance updates are in real time.
Use a message queue for events.

steps.msg: Sam shows the plan and asks: 'Which teams do we depend on, and who depends on us?' The plan has 11 teams, and the dependencies are not written down.

options.t: I'd run a 60-minute session with the team leads and build a dependency map: what each team needs, from whom and by when. I'd mark the ones on the critical path in red and agree on one contact per dependency. We'll review the map every two weeks.
options.c: Сессия с лидерами, карта зависимостей, критический путь и ответственный контакт.

options.t: I'll ask each team to send me their dependencies by email.
options.c: Письма без обсуждения дадут неполные ответы.

options.t: I'll guess the dependencies from the plan.
options.c: Догадки по плану пропустят скрытые зависимости.

options.t: I'll tell Sam that this is a project manager's task.
options.c: Отказ: анализ зависимостей — часть работы BA.

words.ex: Dependencies on the critical path need attention.

steps.msg: In a test migration, 8% of customer records fail: missing birth dates, addresses in free text and duplicate customers. The deadline is in six weeks.

options.t: I'd sort the issues by type and count: missing dates, free text addresses and duplicates. For each I'd propose a rule: fix in the old system, clean with a script, or fix by hand. Then we agree on owners and a daily progress report. We'd aim for under 0.5% failing on the final rehearsal.
options.c: Сортировка проблем, правило для каждого типа, владельцы и целевая доля ошибок.

options.t: I'll ask the developers to skip the failing records.
options.c: Пропуск записей потеряет клиентов.

options.t: I'll ask the branches to fix the records by hand.
options.c: Ручное исправление без приоритетов не успеет за шесть недель.

options.t: I'll ask for a later deadline.
options.c: Сдвиг срока без анализа.

steps.msg: Two teams argue about an interface. The payments team says the new core must send an event 'payment completed'. The core team says: 'We only provide a status that you can read.'

options.t: Let's write the contract together. I'd list what each side needs: what data, how often, how fast, and what happens on failure. Then we choose between event and status, based on the needs, and record the decision. The contract has one owner on each side.
options.c: Совместный контракт: данные, частота, скорость и поведение при сбое; решение по потребностям.

options.t: I'll decide. An event is more modern.
options.c: «Современнее» — не причина.

options.t: Let's compromise: the core sends the event sometimes.
options.c: «Иногда» — неопределённость.

options.t: Let's ask management to decide.
options.c: Эскалация без анализа.

words.how: Соглашение о данных, формате и поведении.
Сообщение о том, что что-то произошло.
Что делать, если интерфейс не отвечает.

steps.msg: After the first parallel run, the old and the new system show different totals for the day: a difference of $12,400 on $8 million. Victor from finance asks: 'Is this a problem?'

options.t: I don't know yet. I'd break the difference down by transaction type and find the biggest part first. I'd send you the first findings by tomorrow morning, with a list of what is explained, what is not, and what could be a rule difference. Until then, I'd not treat it as an acceptable difference.
options.c: Не знает, разбирает по типам операций, обещает первые результаты и пока не считает допустимым.

options.t: It's a small difference, 0.15%. I'd say it's fine.
options.c: Малый процент может скрывать системную ошибку.

options.t: It's a problem. We cannot go live with this.
options.c: Преждевременный вывод без анализа.

options.t: It's probably rounding. I'd ignore it.
options.c: Предположение без проверки.

words.how: Обе системы работают на одних данных для сравнения.
words.ex: The parallel run runs for a month.
Break down the difference by type.

steps.msg: Sam asks you to write the cutover plan for the weekend when the old core is switched off. The plan must cover about 120 steps and 9 teams. You have three weeks.

options.t: I'd write it by time and owner: each step with a start time, duration, owner, check and a stop rule. I'd run a rehearsal in week two, measure the real times, and fix the plan. I'd also mark the rollback point: the last moment when we can safely go back.
options.c: План по времени и владельцам с проверкой и правилом остановки, репетиция и точка отката.

options.t: I'd write a general plan with the main steps. The teams will add details.
options.c: Общий план не проверить и не исполнить.

options.t: I'd copy the plan from the last big release.
options.c: Копия не учитывает специфику.

options.t: I'd write the plan after the rehearsals, when we know the details.
options.c: План после репетиции — нечего репетировать.

words.how: Момент, когда старая система заменяется новой.
words.ex: The cutover is on the weekend.
Define a stop rule for each step.

steps.msg: Alex says: 'For end-to-end testing, we need realistic data, but we cannot use real customer data in the test systems. What do we do?' The test has to start in three weeks.

options.t: I'd propose masked data: take real structures and patterns, replace names, numbers and addresses, and keep the rules, such as account types and balances in the same ranges. Olga must approve the method. If it takes too long, we start with a synthetic set for the main flows.
options.c: Маскированные данные с сохранением правил, согласование с комплаенсом и запасной синтетический набор.

options.t: I'd copy the production data into the test system. It's the most realistic.
options.c: Реальные данные в тесте — нарушение.

options.t: I'd create a small set of data by hand.
options.c: Малый набор не покрывает сценарии.

options.t: I'd test with real data, and ask customers for consent.
options.c: Согласие клиентов не решает риск утечки из тестовой среды.

words.how: Реальные структуры с заменёнными персональными значениями.
Проверка всего пути от начала до конца.

steps.msg: Leo asks you to help document an architecture decision: build the loan scoring in-house or buy a ready solution. The team is divided, and some people have strong opinions.

options.t: I'd write a short decision record: the context, the options, the criteria, and the result of each option. I'd choose four criteria with the team first, such as cost over five years, time to launch, control over the rules, and regulatory fit. Then the decision follows the evidence, and everyone sees why.
options.c: Запись решения: контекст, варианты, критерии и оценка; критерии согласованы заранее.

options.t: I'd vote with the team. The majority decides.
options.c: Голосование не заменяет оценку.

options.t: I'd ask Leo to decide. He's the architect.
options.c: Архитектор принимает решение, но по прозрачным критериям.

options.t: I'd choose buy. It's faster.
options.c: Выбор без критериев.

words.how: Короткий документ: что выбрали и почему.
Что мы используем для сравнения вариантов.

steps.msg: Tom says: 'The new core must handle 300 payments per second on the salary day. Do we know this number?' You do not have it. The business said 'many.'

options.t: I'd ask finance and operations for the last three salary days and the growth forecast, and I'd calculate the peak per second. Then I'd add a safety margin of 50% and state the assumption in the requirement. Until we have data, I'd treat 300 as an assumption, not a fact.
options.c: Берёт данные за последние пики, считает пик в секунду, добавляет запас и маркирует допущение.

options.t: 300 sounds right. Let's use it.
options.c: «Звучит правильно» — не основание.

options.t: Let's design for 1,000 to be safe.
options.c: Завышение без данных увеличивает стоимость.

options.t: Let's wait until we see the real load after launch.
options.c: Ожидание запуска: поздно и рискованно.

steps.msg: The core banking vendor says: "The interface to your card system will be ready two months later than planned." Greg asks you: "Can we still keep our date?"

options.t: I'd check what in our plan depends on that interface and what we can do in the meantime. I'd bring three options by Thursday: a temporary file exchange, a shift of the card migration, or a move of the whole date, with the cost and the risk of each.
options.c: Варианты с ценой и риском.

options.t: I'd ask the vendor if they can speed up. If they say no, we move the date. The vendor wants to keep the contract. A short call could change the date. I'd not ask for a written promise. The vendor often agrees in a short call.
options.c: Просит ускорить.

options.t: I'd say that it depends on the vendor, and I'd wait for their new plan before we decide.
options.c: Ждёт.

options.t: I'd say yes, and tell the vendor that the date cannot change because of the contract.
options.c: Давит.

words.ex: The vendor delay affects the plan.
The card interface is a critical dependency.

steps.msg: The vendor says: "The temporary file exchange is possible, but the files will arrive once a day." Operations says that customers will see old card data for up to 24 hours.

options.t: I'd ask Rita and Olga whether one day of delay is acceptable for card data. If it is, we need three controls: a message in the app, a daily check, and a list of cases with a risk. I'd show them real examples.
options.c: Проверяет допустимость и меры контроля.

options.t: I'd accept the delay, because it is temporary, and we keep the date. We'll inform support about it. The delay is only one day. Support can write a short note. Customers will not see the problem. The risk for customers is small.
options.c: Принимает.

options.t: I'd refuse the daily file because it is a risk, and I'd suggest a delay of the cutover until the real interface is ready. The partner may need more time to finish the interface. A later date gives a calm cutover.
options.c: Отказывается.

options.t: I'd tell the vendor that one day is too long, and ask them to find a better solution.
options.c: Отправляет назад.

words.ex: We use file exchange as a stop-gap.

words.how: Время между событием и доступностью данных.

steps.msg: Max asks you to run a short training for six junior analysts about writing interface requirements. You have 90 minutes. Most of them have never seen an API.

options.t: I'd split it into three parts: 20 minutes to explain what an API is with a simple example, 40 minutes to write a small interface requirement together in groups, and 30 minutes for feedback and questions. I'd give a one-page template.
options.c: План, практика и шаблон.

options.t: I'd show a presentation about API basics and finish with questions, because the topic is new to them.
options.c: Только лекция.

options.t: I'd give them a technical document about the API of our new core and ask them to read it. It has all the details. The juniors can find what they need. I'd mark the important pages. The document is in the shared drive.
options.c: Документ.

options.t: I'd say that it is too early for them, and they should first learn the basics from developers.
options.c: Откладывает.

steps.msg: After the training, one junior writes: "I understood the idea, but I still cannot imagine what to ask the developers." She is honest and a little embarrassed.

options.t: Thank you for saying it. A good way is a list of five questions: what comes in, what comes out, what can fail, how fast it must be, and who owns it. Let's sit together for 30 minutes on a real example and use these questions.
options.c: Список вопросов и практика.

options.t: Don't worry, it comes with practice. I'd suggest that you join a meeting with the developers and listen. Every analyst starts like this. The developers are friendly. Maybe you can bring a notebook. The project can be a good start.
options.c: Только наблюдать.

options.t: I'd send you the training slides again, so that you can look through them in your own time.
options.c: Те же слайды.

options.t: I'd say that you should ask the developers to explain it to you. They know the details better.
options.c: Перекладывает.

words.how: Что передаётся в систему и что возвращается.

steps.msg: It is Thursday, 48 hours before the cutover of the core banking system. The last rehearsal showed: the migration took 31 hours instead of 24, the card interface works with a daily file, and 3 of 40 test scenarios fail. Marcus asks the leads in a call: "Are we ready? Yes or no?"

options.t: I'd answer with facts first: the migration is 7 hours longer than planned, the 3 failed scenarios are in payments, and the card file is a known limit. My recommendation depends on two things: can we fix the payment scenarios by tomorrow noon, and does the weekend give us 31 hours? I'd bring a go or no-go answer at 2 p.m. tomorrow.
options.c: Факты, условия и срок ответа.
options.r: Marcus hears the real picture and sets a time for a decision, and the team gets time to prepare.

options.t: We are almost ready. The three failed scenarios are being fixed, and the longer time is a result of the load on the test system. I'd say that I'm optimistic. The test system is slow on Thursdays. I'd write the status in green. Marcus likes good news. Customers are not interested in test results. The failed scenarios are minor. A short email to the board is enough.
options.c: Оптимизм без оснований.
options.r: Marcus hears a positive message, but Tom disagrees, and the call becomes confused.

options.t: It is a decision for the business. I'd tell him that the project team will do what is needed, and the risks are on the list.
options.c: Отходит.
options.r: Marcus asks again, and no one gives a clear answer.

options.t: Yes, we are ready. Every cutover has small problems, and we can solve them during the weekend.
options.c: Говорит «да».
options.r: Marcus approves the plan, and the real risks stay hidden.

steps.explain: Перед решением go/no-go говорите фактами и условиями, а не «да» или «нет» без оснований. Назовите, что должно быть выполнено и когда будет ответ.

words.ex: The go/no-go meeting is on Thursday.
The last rehearsal was too long.

steps.msg: On Friday at noon, the payment scenarios are fixed. The migration time was cut to 27 hours with a script change. The weekend window is 30 hours. Nina says the margin is thin. Olga says: "If it fails in the middle, a rollback needs 10 hours." Marcus asks for your recommendation.

options.t: I'd recommend go, with three conditions: a rollback decision point at hour 18, an extra 4 hours of buffer on Monday morning, and a customer message ready for both outcomes. The risk is thin margin, and the rollback needs 10 hours, so the decision point must be strict.
options.c: Рекомендация с условиями и точкой отката.
options.r: Marcus accepts the plan, and the team knows exactly when to stop.

options.t: I'd recommend go. The fix is done, the timing is within the window, and further delay costs money.
options.c: Без условий.
options.r: Marcus approves, but nobody has a clear rule for a rollback.

options.t: I'd recommend a delay by one month. The margin is thin, and it is better to be safe. Marcus will understand one month. The team can use the time for tests. A short delay is better than a long outage.
options.c: Откладывает.
options.r: Marcus is unhappy about the delay, and the team loses momentum.

options.t: I'd say that both choices have risks, and it is a business decision. Marcus should decide.
options.c: Отказывается рекомендовать.
options.r: Marcus decides without your input, and he feels left alone.

steps.explain: Рекомендация должна содержать решение, условия и точку отката. Назовите риск и срок, когда вы остановите процесс.

words.how: Условия, при которых можно идти дальше.

steps.msg: At hour 17 on Saturday, the migration shows a mismatch in loan balances: 2,300 loans have a different interest amount. Tom says it may be a rounding issue. The decision point is in one hour.

options.t: I'd use the hour to check a sample of 100 loans, to see if the difference is the same rounding rule and how big it is. If the sample shows a small and known cause, we continue and fix later. If we see unknown causes or big amounts, I'd recommend a rollback at hour 18.
options.c: Использует час для выборки, правило остановки.
options.r: The sample gives a clear answer, and the team decides on facts at the decision point.

options.t: I'd continue because the cause is probably rounding, as Tom says. We can correct it after the migration.
options.c: Верит версии.
options.r: The migration continues, but a bigger cause might be hidden.

options.t: I'd stop now and roll back. 2,300 loans are too many to risk, and it's safer to try again later. The next try can be in two weeks. The weekend has no new work. Marcus can wait one more week.
options.c: Откатывает рано.
options.r: The team loses the weekend, and the second attempt needs a new plan.

options.t: I'd tell Marcus about it and ask him to decide whether to continue. It is a big decision. He decides on such questions. I'd give him all the facts. I'd say that both options are possible.
options.c: Передаёт CEO.
options.r: Marcus has no facts, and the decision point passes without a clear answer.

steps.explain: Если рядом точка решения, используйте оставшееся время для проверки выборки. Держитесь заранее согласованного правила остановки.

words.how: Различие между старыми и новыми значениями.
words.ex: There is a mismatch in interest.
Run a sample check of 100 loans.

steps.msg: On Monday morning, customers log in. The system works, and support sees a small number of calls about wrong interest for 140 loans. Marcus asks you what to do now.

options.t: I'd have a list of the 140 loans from the check, fix the interest by script today, and send each customer a short message that explains the correction. I'd ask Olga to review the text. I'd also write a short report for you on what we learned, with actions.
options.c: Список, скрипт, сообщение, отчёт.
options.r: Customers receive a clear message, and the issue is closed within a day.

options.t: I'd fix the loans first and tell customers if they call. We should not make a bigger problem than it is. Most customers will not call. The loans can be fixed one by one. I'd keep the message short.
options.c: Молчит.
options.r: Some customers notice the difference on their own and lose trust.

options.t: I'd ask support to explain to callers that the system is new and small problems may happen.
options.c: Общее объяснение.
options.r: Customers hear a general reason and ask for details again.

options.t: I'd wait to see how many customers call and fix the loans one by one when they complain. Complaints show real cases. A list of loans costs hours. Most customers will not notice a small interest change.
options.c: Ждёт жалоб.
options.r: The number of complaints grows, and the bank looks careless.

steps.explain: Если после запуска нашли ошибки, исправьте их по списку, сообщите клиентам и подготовьте короткий отчёт о выводах.

endings.good: You made a clear, honest recommendation based on facts. The decision is taken with full information, and customers and the team are protected.
endings.mid: The decision is taken, but with unclear information, so the weekend is stressful, and some customers have problems.
endings.bad: The cutover happens with hidden risks, and it ends with a long outage and a crisis for the whole bank.

steps.msg: After the migration, the month-end report in the new system shows an interest income of $2.31 million. Finance's own calculation says $2.38 million. Victor writes: "I need to sign the month-end in three days. Which number is correct?"

options.t: I don't know yet, and I won't guess. I'd compare the two at loan level for a sample, find the biggest differences and give you a first explanation tomorrow. By day two, I'd give you a clear status: a closed cause or an open list.
options.c: Не гадает, даёт этапы и срок.
options.r: Victor sees a plan with milestones, and he can plan the sign-off.

options.t: I think the new system is correct, because it uses the same rules as before. I'd double-check and tell you later. The old system was tested for years. I'd ask Tom to check the rule again. Finance can wait one day.
options.c: Защищает систему.
options.r: Victor waits, but he is not sure if he can trust the answer.

options.t: The difference is only 3%. I'd use the finance number for the report and fix the system later.
options.c: Берёт цифру финансов.
options.r: The report is signed, and the new system keeps the gap.

options.t: I'd ask Victor to sign using the system number, because it is the official source.
options.c: Давит.
options.r: Victor refuses to sign, and the trust in the new system falls.

steps.explain: При расхождении между системой и финансами не гадайте. Сравните на уровне отдельных записей, назовите этапы и срок.

words.ex: Month-end close uses the new report.

steps.msg: The comparison shows that most of the difference is in loans paid early. The new system calculates interest to the day of repayment. Finance's old rule counts a full month. The difference is $55,000. The rest of the gap, $15,000, has no explanation.

options.t: I'd explain the $55,000 as a rule difference and ask Victor and Olga which rule is correct by contract and policy. For the $15,000 I'd keep a clear open item with a plan: a loan-by-loan check by Friday. I'd not close the gap by an adjustment.
options.c: Объясняет часть, остальное остаётся открытым.
options.r: Victor knows exactly what is explained and what is not, and he can sign with a note.

options.t: I'd say that the $55,000 is a known difference and that the rest is small. We can sign with a note about the open amount. The $15,000 is under half a percent. Victor can accept a note. I'd not open a new check. I'd write the same in the report.
options.c: Минимизирует остаток.
options.r: Victor signs, but the open amount is not tracked.

options.t: I'd add a manual adjustment of $15,000 so that the numbers match, and fix the cause later.
options.c: Подгоняет.
options.r: The numbers match, and the real cause stays hidden.

options.t: I'd say that all differences are due to the rule, and the report is correct.
options.c: Всё объясняет правилом.
options.r: The unexplained part comes back next month and is bigger.

steps.explain: Объясните то, что понятно, и оставьте открытыми то, что неясно. Не подгоняйте цифры корректировкой.

steps.msg: Next month, the same gap appears again, but the rule difference is gone. Victor asks: "How do we stop this from repeating every month?"

options.t: I'd build a reconciliation report that compares the system and finance by product every day, with a limit of 0.1% and a list of loans above the limit. I'd name an owner in finance and an owner in IT, and review the top causes each month.
options.c: Ежедневная сверка, лимит, владельцы.
options.r: Finance and IT agree on owners, and the monthly gap shrinks fast.

options.t: I'd ask finance to do the check by themselves each month and tell us about any difference.
options.c: Перекладывает.
options.r: Finance does its own checks, but IT does not see the problems early.

options.t: I'd write the month-end rules in a document, so that both teams use the same logic. A document is clear for both teams. The same logic is easy to follow. It needs no extra tools.
options.c: Документ без контроля.
options.r: Both teams read the document, but the gaps keep appearing.

options.t: I'd wait until the system is more stable, and the differences will reduce by themselves.
options.c: Ждёт.
options.r: The gaps continue, and finance builds a separate report.

steps.explain: Чтобы расхождения не повторялись, настройте регулярную сверку с порогом и назначьте владельцев с обеих сторон.

endings.good: You found the cause, fixed the rule and made the numbers match. Finance trusts the new system and the process.
endings.mid: The numbers match for now, but the cause is not fully understood, and a similar gap may come back.
endings.bad: Finance does not trust the new reports and builds its own, and the two worlds drift apart.

steps.msg: You lead 14 analysts. Their documents look different: some write long specs, some write only short notes, and developers complain. You want to introduce a standard without killing creativity.

options.t: I'd agree on a small core that every document must have: goal, scope, main flows, rules, non-functional needs and open questions. Beyond that, analysts choose the format that fits. I'd pilot it for a month with three people, collect feedback from developers, and then make it official.
options.c: Малое обязательное ядро, свобода сверху, пилот и обратная связь от разработчиков.

options.t: I'd introduce a strict 40-page template for everyone.
options.c: Длинный шаблон создаёт формализм.

options.t: I'd let each analyst keep their style. Developers should adapt.
options.c: Без стандарта жалобы останутся.

options.t: I'd choose the best analyst's style and make it the standard.
options.c: Стиль одного человека не подходит всем проектам.

words.ex: Every document has the same core.
Build a feedback loop with developers.

steps.msg: You can hire two analysts. You have 40 applicants. One is a strong business analyst with banking experience but weak technical skills. Another is a systems analyst with strong API and data skills but no banking background.

options.t: I'd look at what the team lacks today. We have strong banking knowledge but little API and data skills, so I'd hire the systems analyst and pair them with a banking mentor for six months. For the second place, I'd decide after interviews for the cultural fit and potential.
options.c: Анализирует пробелы команды, берёт системного аналитика и планирует наставника.

options.t: I'd hire both. They complement each other.
options.c: Оба — бюджет на двоих не позволяет, и не оценено, чего не хватает.

options.t: I'd hire the one with banking experience. Banking knowledge is hard to learn.
options.c: Знание банка — важно, но не единственное.

options.t: I'd hire the one with technical skills. They are easier to train.
options.c: Технические навыки — не всегда проще.

words.ex: Hire to close the skill gap.

steps.msg: Zoe, a good analyst with three years of experience, asks: 'What do I need to do to become senior? I don't see clear criteria.' You do not have a written ladder.

options.t: It's a fair question. I'd write a simple ladder with levels and examples: what scope you own, how complex the problems are, and how you help others. I'll share a draft with you in two weeks and ask you to comment. Meanwhile, let's pick two goals for the next six months that move you toward senior.
options.c: Признаёт отсутствие критериев, обещает черновик лестницы и ставит две цели на полгода.

options.t: You need two more years of experience. It's how it works.
options.c: Стаж — не критерий роста.

options.t: Just work harder, and you'll be promoted when it's time.
options.c: Туманный совет без критериев.

options.t: I'll promote you when a senior position opens.
options.c: Привязка к вакансии: нет роста без места.

words.ex: Senior analysts own a larger scope.

steps.msg: One of your analysts has missed three deadlines in two months, and his documents have many gaps. Developers complain about him. He is also going through a divorce, and you know it.

options.t: I'd have a private conversation: say what I see with two or three examples, ask what is happening, and listen. Then we agree on a clear plan with small steps and weekly check-ins, and I'd offer support: lighter workload for a month and the employee assistance program. I'd document it, with his agreement.
options.c: Личный разговор с примерами, слушание, план шагов, поддержка и фиксация.

options.t: I'd give him a formal warning. His results are not acceptable.
options.c: Официальное предупреждение без разговора и помощи.

options.t: I'd ignore it. He has personal problems, and it's not my business.
options.c: Игнорирование: страдают команда и он сам.

options.t: I'd move him to a simpler project without talking to him.
options.c: Решение без него разрушит доверие.

steps.msg: Seven projects ask for analysts, and you have capacity for four. Marcus says: 'All of them are important.' Each project owner insists on their own.

options.t: I'd make one page: for each project, the goal, the value, the deadline, and what happens if we delay. I'd rank them with simple criteria such as regulatory date, revenue or savings, and customer impact. Then I'd bring the ranking to you and the owners, and we'd challenge it together before the decision.
options.c: Одна страница, критерии, последствия задержки и общее обсуждение ранжирования.

options.t: I'd pick the four projects with the loudest owners.
options.c: Громкость не равна ценности.

options.t: I'd split the analysts across all seven projects.
options.c: Размытие мощности: ни один проект не получит достаточно.

options.t: I'd ask the project owners to agree among themselves.
options.c: Договорённость владельцев — конфликт интересов.

steps.msg: Tom says: 'Analysts write long documents nobody reads. In agile we need just user stories. Let's stop the documents.' Some of your analysts disagree strongly.

options.t: I agree that long documents are a waste. But some things must be written: rules, interfaces and decisions, because teams and auditors need them. I'd propose living documents, short and updated with each sprint, and stories that link to them. We keep what is used and drop what is not.
options.c: Согласен с критикой, сохраняет правила, интерфейсы и решения и предлагает живые документы.

options.t: I disagree. We need complete documents for every project.
options.c: Полные документы повторят проблему.

options.t: I agree. Let's stop writing documents.
options.c: Полный отказ оставит аудиторов и команды без источника правды.

options.t: Let's ask the developers what they want.
options.c: Мнение разработчиков важно, но не единственное.

words.how: Короткий документ, который обновляют вместе с продуктом.

words.ex: The auditor needs the decision log.

steps.msg: The analysts use three tools for requirements: Word, a wiki and Jira. Greg wants one tool and asks you to propose. The team has strong preferences.

options.t: I'd start from the needs: traceability, easy reading for developers, versions and access control. I'd test two tools with one project for a month, and ask the team to rate them on these needs. Then I'd show Greg the results and the cost of moving. We'd keep the old documents readable during the migration.
options.c: Потребности, пилот двух инструментов, оценка командой, цена перехода и сохранение старых документов.

options.t: I'd choose Jira. Developers already use it.
options.c: Выбор по привычке без проверки потребностей.

options.t: I'd choose the cheapest tool.
options.c: Цена — не единственный критерий.

options.t: I'd let each analyst keep their tool. It's their choice.
options.c: Три инструмента: проблема останется.

words.how: Связь требований с тестами и задачами.

steps.msg: Greg asks: 'Can we use an AI assistant to write requirements? It could save 30% of the time.' Your analysts are worried and curious. The documents contain confidential bank information.

options.t: Yes, with rules. First we check the data policy with Olga, and use only approved tools. Then we test it on drafts, with a human check of each output. We'd track time saved and errors found for two months. The analyst remains responsible for every requirement.
options.c: С правилами: утверждённые инструменты, проверка человеком, метрики и ответственность аналитика.

options.t: Yes, let everyone use any AI tool they like.
options.c: Любые инструменты: риск утечки.

options.t: No. AI will make mistakes and leak data.
options.c: Полный отказ упускает пользу.

options.t: Yes, and let AI write all the requirements.
options.c: Полная замена опасна: ответственность остаётся у человека.

words.how: Инструмент, помогающий писать тексты и код.

steps.msg: Victor says that an outside company offers analysts at 40% less than your team's cost. He asks: 'Why don't we outsource part of the work?' You know that outsourcing has risks.

options.t: It is worth looking at. I'd suggest that we split the work: routine work, such as documenting stable processes, may go to outsiders, while new products and sensitive topics stay with us. We'd run a three-month trial with clear quality measures, and compare the real cost, including management time, not only the rate.
options.c: Разделение рутины и чувствительной работы, пилот три месяца, реальная стоимость с управлением.

options.t: No. Outsourcing never works. The quality is poor.
options.c: Категорический отказ без анализа.

options.t: Yes, let's outsource everything. It saves 40%.
options.c: Весь объём: потеря знаний и контроля.

options.t: Let's outsource the work, and keep only the managers.
options.c: Только менеджеры: некому знать банк.

words.ex: Routine work is easier to outsource.

steps.msg: Marcus asks: 'How do I know that my analysts do a good job? Give me three numbers.' It is hard to measure the work of analysts.

options.t: I'd offer three simple measures: how many requirements change after development starts, how many defects come from unclear requirements, and how developers and business rate our work in a short survey. I'd show trends, not single points, and I'd agree on targets with you and the team.
options.c: Три показателя качества: изменения после старта, дефекты из-за требований, оценка заказчиков; тренды и цели.

options.t: I'd give you the number of documents written. It's easy to count.
options.c: Число документов не показывает качества.

options.t: I'd give you the number of hours worked.
options.c: Часы не показывают результата.

options.t: I'd say it can't be measured. Trust me.
options.c: «Верьте» не работает для CEO.

words.how: Доля требований, изменённых после начала разработки.

steps.msg: Marcus says in front of the executives: "I don't understand why analysts need three months to write requirements for a small feature. My son built an app in a weekend." People look at you.

options.t: I understand the frustration. Let me explain what the three months include: talking to customers and operations, checking rules with compliance, and agreeing interfaces. I'd propose a simple test: for the next small feature, I'd show you a timeline, and we look for steps that can be shorter.
options.c: Объясняет и предлагает проверку.

options.t: It is a different kind of work. A bank has regulation, and an app for a weekend has none. I'd be happy to explain it later. It is not easy to compare. The CEO's son uses a free tool. I'd draw a short diagram next time.
options.c: Объясняет отличие.

options.t: I'd say that the analysts work hard, and the timeline is realistic. If we rush, the quality will fall.
options.c: Защищается.

options.t: I'd say nothing in the meeting and talk with Marcus in private. It's better not to argue with the CEO in public. The CEO is under stress today. The meeting is short. I'd keep my comment for the break.
options.c: Молчит.

words.ex: Show the timeline of the analysis.
The analysis phase takes three months.

steps.msg: After the meeting, Marcus says: "Fine. Show me the timeline for the next feature. And I want weekly updates." He is not smiling.

options.t: Thank you. I'd send a one-page timeline by Friday, with each step, who owns it, and the days. I'd mark the steps where we can save time, and the ones that protect customers and the bank. Weekly updates are fine, and I'd keep them short.
options.c: Конкретный план и обновления.

options.t: I will do that. Weekly updates may take time from the team, so I'd ask Marcus to accept updates every two weeks.
options.c: Просит реже.

options.t: I'd send the timeline and the updates, but I'd also write a note to explain why it is not good to put pressure on the analysts. Marcus should know the effect of his request. I'd send the note to Helen too. It is better to say it in writing.
options.c: Жалуется.

options.t: I'd say that it is not necessary to have weekly updates, because the team is working well. Marcus can see the board anytime. Updates take time from the team. A monthly note is enough.
options.c: Отказывается.

steps.msg: Max, your best senior analyst and the mentor of half of the team, says he wants to leave in a month. He has an offer from a fintech company with a 30% higher salary and a title of lead.

options.t: Thank you for telling me directly. I don't want to lose you, and I understand the offer. I can't match the whole package, but I can give you a lead role in the new program, a salary review in the next cycle and time for mentoring. What would make you stay?
options.c: Признаёт, предлагает реальное.

options.t: I'm sorry to hear that. Let me talk to Marcus about a raise today. I'm sure we can find a solution. You have a strong record. The offer is high, but money is not everything. I'd talk to him today. I'd write the offer in an email. He is important for the team.
options.c: Обещает.

options.t: I understand. It is a great opportunity, and I wish you success. I'd ask you to prepare a handover for your projects.
options.c: Принимает.

options.t: I'm disappointed. The team needs you now, and the timing is difficult. I hope that you will think about it.
options.c: Давит.

words.ex: The compensation is below the market.
Offer a bigger scope of work.

steps.msg: Max says: "It is not only money. I want to build products, not only write requirements. I think that I will leave anyway." He is calm.

options.t: Thank you for being honest. If you leave, I'd like it to be a good move for you and for the team. I'd ask you to prepare a handover plan with the team, and I'd offer you to be an advisor for the first three months. Let's keep in touch.
options.c: Достойный переход.

options.t: Let me think if there is a product role at Nordline. I'd talk to Helen, and we can see if there is a place for you. A product role needs a long process. Max is a good fit for it. I'd tell him in the next call. It is not the first time he asks.
options.c: Ищет вариант.

options.t: I understand. I'd ask you to stay for two months to finish the current projects. The projects need a clean handover. Your team members can learn from you. Two months pass quickly.
options.c: Просит остаться на срок.

options.t: I'd say that it is a pity. I thought that you were committed to the team, and I am surprised.
options.c: Обижается.

words.ex: Keep him in the alumni network.

steps.msg: Three executives ask for analysts at the same time. Olga needs two analysts for a new regulation, due in four months. Helen needs three for a new loan product, and the marketing head needs one for a campaign. You have five free analysts and eight requests.

options.t: I'd collect the three requests in one table: the goal, the deadline, the people needed and the cost of a delay. Regulation has a legal date, so it goes first. I'd propose a plan to Marcus, with the trade-offs, and I'd meet the three executives together.
options.c: Единая таблица, предлагает план.
options.r: The executives see the same table, and the discussion moves to facts.

options.t: I'd give the analysts to the executive who asked first, because it is a fair rule and easy to explain.
options.c: Первый пришёл.
options.r: Two executives feel it is unfair, and they go to Marcus.

options.t: I'd ask Marcus to decide, because he sees the whole picture and the priorities of the bank. He knows the budget. The choice affects the whole bank. I'd send him the list tonight. He also knows the team.
options.c: Передаёт CEO.
options.r: Marcus is irritated that he has no recommendation, and the decision is slow.

options.t: I'd say yes to all three and split the analysts, so that nobody is left without help.
options.c: Раздаёт всем.
options.r: Every project gets a part of an analyst, and nothing moves fast.

steps.explain: При нехватке ресурсов соберите все запросы в одну таблицу с целью, сроком и ценой задержки. Предложите план и соберите руководителей на одну встречу.

steps.msg: The regulation gets two analysts, Helen's product gets three, and marketing gets none. The marketing head is angry: "My campaign is worth $2 million. You decided that it does not matter?"

options.t: I understand that it is frustrating. The campaign matters, but the analyst capacity is full until October. I'd offer a light version: a template for the requirements that your team fills in, and two hours of my time each week for review. If the plan changes, you're first on the list.
options.c: Предлагает лёгкий вариант.
options.r: The marketing head still disagrees, but she accepts a light plan and a place in the queue.

options.t: I'm sorry, but the decision is made. I'd suggest that you ask Marcus if he wants to change the priorities. Marcus has seen the plan. A new request now would break the team's schedule. I will talk to you again next week.
options.c: Отправляет к CEO.
options.r: She goes to Marcus, and he asks you why the plan was not explained better.

options.t: I'd give you one analyst for one month, to calm the situation, and I'd take it from Helen's team. One analyst is enough for the first step. Helen's team has a smaller load now. I'd move her on Monday. She can start the next day.
options.c: Уступает.
