steps.msg: Carlos says the team's pace is unstable because releases always get rushed at the end. He asks what you will change in the way product plans work.

options.t: Introduce a planning rule: fix the release scope two weeks before the date, keep a small reserve for surprises, and accept no new requests after that.
options.c: Системно убирает причину спешки.
options.r: Releases become calmer, and the team knows what to expect.

options.t: Add a daily progress meeting for everyone, so you can catch delays earlier.
options.c: Больше встреч, но причина спешки та же.
options.r: The team spends more time in meetings, and the pressure stays.

options.t: Keep the current process, and remind everyone to plan better.
options.c: Призыв без изменений ничего не меняет.
options.r: Nothing changes, and the next release is rushed again.

options.t: Ask each PM to plan with a buffer, but leave the rules to them.
options.c: Помогает, но без общего правила каждый делает по-своему.
options.r: Some teams plan well, others do not, and the rushing continues in several places.

words.ex: Add a buffer to every plan.

words.how: Момент, после которого новые требования не принимают.
words.ex: Scope freeze is two weeks before release.

steps.msg: Three months later, Ira is doing well. A newer engineer, Dev, now shows the same signs of exhaustion. Carlos asks how you want to handle it this time.

options.t: Do not wait for a crisis: check in with Dev, review the team's workload every month, and ask Carlos to share early warning signs with you.
options.c: Переходит от реакции к профилактике.
options.r: Dev gets support early, and the team starts to treat workload as something to discuss openly.

options.t: Remind Carlos that you solved this once, and ask him to handle it the same way.
options.c: Опирается на опыт, но систему не меняет.
options.r: It works for Dev, but the next person will face the same problem.

options.t: Leave it to Dev to ask for help if he needs it.
options.c: Выгорающие люди редко просят о помощи сами.
options.r: Dev stays silent for weeks, and the quality of his work drops.

options.t: Suggest a team survey about workload once a quarter, and discuss the results.
options.c: Полезно, но реагирует слишком редко.
options.r: The survey brings useful information, but it comes too late for Dev.

words.how: Признак проблемы до того, как она стала кризисом.
words.ex: Silence can be an early warning.

endings.good: Revenue grows without a customer revolt. The bank keeps its reputation, and your phased plan becomes the template for future pricing decisions.
endings.mid: Revenue grows, but trust and retention take a hit that will take time to repair. The CEO is happy with the numbers and uneasy about the news.
endings.bad: The fee increase backfires: customers leave, the press is critical, and the bank has to reverse course. Leadership loses confidence in pricing decisions.

steps.msg: Priya: 'Leadership wants to raise monthly account fees by 20% next month to hit the revenue target. Our interviews say some customers are already unhappy with fees. What is your first move?'

options.t: Ask Priya to segment customers by value and fee sensitivity, and check how past fee changes affected closed accounts.
options.c: Смотрит на сегменты и историю реакций до решения.
options.r: The data shows that heavy users accept small changes, but a group of low-balance customers is very sensitive.

options.t: Raise the fee by 10% for everyone now, and check the reaction after a month.
options.c: Разумный шаг, но без анализа сегментов он вслепую.
options.r: Revenue rises a little, but some customers complain, and a few close their accounts.

options.t: Raise the fee by 20% for everyone next month as leadership asked, and tell customers by email.
options.c: Быстрая выручка за счёт доверия и удержания.
options.r: Revenue jumps for a month, then thousands of customers close accounts and post angry reviews.

options.t: Tell leadership you need two weeks to analyze the effect before you recommend anything.
options.c: Верное направление, но без плана и без альтернатив.
options.r: Leadership agrees to wait, but wants options when the time comes.

words.ex: The monthly fee is going up.

words.how: Насколько сильно спрос зависит от изменения цены.
words.ex: Price elasticity is high for small accounts.

steps.msg: Interviews with 12 customers show that most would accept a higher fee if they got something clear in return. Basic-plan customers are the most upset, and a competitor advertises zero fees.
steps.alt: The first reaction was rough: complaints are up. Interviews with 12 customers show that most would accept a higher fee if they got something clear in return. Basic-plan customers are the most upset, and a competitor advertises zero fees.

options.t: Propose a smaller increase tied to a visible benefit, like free transfers or cashback, and protect the basic plan.
options.c: Связывает цену с ценностью и защищает чувствительных клиентов.
options.r: Customers see what they receive for the higher fee, and basic-plan customers stay calm.

options.t: Raise fees only for premium customers, and leave the basic plan unchanged, without adding benefits.
options.c: Защищает базовых клиентов, но премиум платит без ценности.
options.r: Premium customers feel they pay more for nothing, and some start comparing alternatives.

options.t: Ignore the competitor's zero fees, since customers do not switch banks easily.
options.c: Недооценивает риск ухода клиентов.
options.r: A few customers leave, and the competitor's ads reach more people than you expected.

options.t: Match the competitor with zero fees on the basic plan, and try to recover revenue from premium services.
options.c: Смелый шаг, но выручка под вопросом.
options.r: Customers are happy, but the revenue target is far away, and finance is worried.

words.ex: Cashback makes the fee easier to accept.

steps.msg: Leadership still wants a revenue boost this quarter. You can present a plan, but the CEO will decide in a single meeting.

options.t: Present three options with revenue, risk and customer impact, recommend a phased increase with benefits, and show how you will measure each stage.
options.c: Даёт варианты, рекомендацию и способ измерения.
options.r: The CEO chooses your recommended plan and sets clear checkpoints for the next quarter.

options.t: Present one option only, the 20% increase, with a warning about the risks.
options.c: Выбора для руководства нет, риски остаются на бумаге.
options.r: The CEO approves the 20% increase, since there was no alternative.

options.t: Say that the revenue target should be lowered because customers cannot pay more.
options.c: Отказывается решать задачу, предлагая снизить цель.
options.r: The CEO feels you are not helping with the target, and the meeting becomes tense.

options.t: Present two options with revenue numbers and mention customer risks briefly.
options.c: Хорошо, но риски для клиентов раскрыты слабо.
options.r: The CEO picks the higher-revenue option, and the customer risk is underestimated.

words.how: Рост цены частями, а не сразу.
Момент, когда проверяют результаты и решают дальше.
words.ex: We set a checkpoint after one month.

steps.msg: The first stage goes live. Support reports a spike in questions about the new fee, and a news site writes a short critical article.

options.t: Publish a clear explanation on the website and in the app, train support with simple answers, and reply to the article with facts and the benefits you added.
options.c: Прозрачное объяснение и готовая поддержка.
options.r: Complaints peak and fall within a week, and the article is forgotten.

options.t: Say nothing publicly and wait for the interest to fade.
options.c: Тишина оставляет место чужим версиям.
options.r: Customers fill the silence with worse stories, and support is overwhelmed.

options.t: Reverse the fee increase immediately to stop the criticism.
options.c: Резкий откат подрывает доверие к решениям банка.
options.r: Critics are quiet for a day, but leadership loses faith in the plan, and revenue falls short.

options.t: Ask support to answer questions one by one, and prepare a longer explanation next week.
options.c: Работает, но поздно и разрозненно.
options.r: Some customers get answers, but the story spreads while the explanation is not ready.

words.ex: There was a spike in support calls.
The bank had to reverse the change.

steps.msg: Two months later, fee revenue is up 9% and closed accounts are slightly above normal. The CEO asks whether to continue to the second stage next month.

options.t: Check retention by customer group first, then continue only for groups that stayed stable, and keep the benefits visible.
options.c: Решение принимается на данных об удержании.
options.r: The second stage works for stable groups, retention holds, and trust is not damaged.

options.t: Continue to the second stage for everyone, since revenue is already moving in the right direction.
options.c: Рост выручки не гарантирует, что клиенты остаются.
options.r: Revenue grows a bit more, but some groups quietly leave, and the damage shows up later.

options.t: Push the full 20% increase now, since the first stage showed that customers accept change.
options.c: Спешка превращает контролируемый тест в риск.
options.r: A bigger wave of customers closes accounts, and the news returns with a bigger story.

options.t: Pause for one quarter to watch retention, and decide later.
options.c: Осторожно, но теряет темп и выручку.
options.r: Retention looks fine, but customers feel the bank is indecisive, and the revenue goal moves further away.

words.how: Доля клиентов, которые уходят за период.
words.ex: Churn rose slightly after the change.
We need a rollout plan for stage two.

endings.good: Your careful work saves the bank from a weak rollout. The VP trusts your numbers, and the team gets a simple testing standard that other teams adopt.
endings.mid: The bank avoids the worst mistake, but the process is slower or less clear than it could be. Your credibility is fine, and the relationship with the VP needs care.
endings.bad: A weak result goes live, and the bank notices it only after complaints arrive. People start to question the data, and the VP relationship is damaged.

steps.msg: The VP of Retail ran an A/B test for three days on a loan offer banner. Version B has 6% more clicks, and she wants to roll it out to all customers today. Nora asks you to prepare a view for the 4 pm meeting.

options.t: Check the sample size, the test length and the metric. Then tell the VP the result is promising but too early, and suggest running the test for two full weeks.
options.c: Проверяет выборку и метрику и предлагает довести тест до конца.
options.r: The VP appreciates the clear reasoning, and the team keeps the test running.

options.t: Tell the VP the result looks good, and promise to check the details after the rollout starts.
options.c: Проверка после запуска приходит слишком поздно.
options.r: The VP is pleased, but you start the rollout before knowing whether the result is real.

options.t: Roll out version B to everyone today, since the VP asked and 6% is a clear win.
options.c: Выкатка без проверки подрывает данные и доверие.
options.r: The VP is happy for a day. A week later the numbers fall back, and your analysis is questioned.

options.t: Ask Nora to move the meeting, and extend the test by a week while you check results for different customer groups.
options.c: Хорошо, но руководителю нужно объяснить причину.
options.r: The extra week gives better data, and the VP accepts it after a short explanation.

words.ex: A small sample size can mislead us.
We planned a rollout for next week.

steps.msg: The extended test ends. B is up 2% in clicks, but loan applications from B are 5% lower and complaints about unclear terms rose. The VP asks, 'So did it work?'
steps.alt: The VP started the rollout early. B is up 2% in clicks, but loan applications are 5% lower and complaints about unclear terms rose. The VP asks, 'So did it work?'

options.t: Explain that clicks are not the goal: applications are lower, so B attracts attention but hurts results. Suggest a clearer version C.
options.c: Смотрит на целевую метрику, а не на клики.
options.r: The VP sees the full picture, and she approves a new test with a clearer banner.

options.t: Say the result is mixed, and show only the click numbers in the report.
options.c: Выбирает удобные цифры вместо полной картины.
options.r: The report looks positive, but the missing numbers will cause trouble later.

options.t: Blame the design team for the unclear terms in version B.
options.c: Перекладывание вины портит отношения и не решает проблему.
options.r: The VP sees you avoid the question, and design stops supporting your tests.

options.t: Show the full numbers and recommend keeping version A, without suggesting what to test next.
options.c: Честно, но без следующего шага.
options.r: The VP accepts it, but she wants to know what comes next, and you have no plan.

words.how: Главный показатель, по которому оценивают успех.
Условия продукта, которые клиент плохо понимает.

steps.msg: Nora asks how you will make sure the bank's future tests are reliable. The VP wants faster results, and the data team wants strict rules.

options.t: Create a short checklist for every test: goal, main metric, sample size, minimum duration and a guardrail metric, reviewed by data before launch.
options.c: Лёгкий общий стандарт, который защищает от ошибок.
options.r: Tests become reliable and quick to approve, and the VP likes having a clear process.

options.t: Ask data to approve every test personally, and allow no test without a formal review.
options.c: Надёжно, но создаёт очередь и тормозит всех.
options.r: Quality improves, but every test waits in a queue and the VP is unhappy.

options.t: Let each team run tests its own way, and ask data to check only the final results.
options.c: Проверка в конце не исправит ошибки в дизайне теста.
options.r: Tests multiply with different rules, and nobody trusts the numbers.

options.t: Ask data to write a long testing guide and share it with all teams next quarter.
options.c: Полезно, но долго, и мало кто прочитает.
options.r: The guide is thorough, but most teams do not read it, and the mistakes continue.

words.how: Показатель, который не должен ухудшиться из-за теста.

words.ex: Use the checklist before every test.

endings.good: Both clients stay and become advocates. Engineering keeps its focus, and Ben learns to bring you client problems early instead of promises.
endings.mid: Both clients stay for now, but one of them is less happy than it should be, and some engineering time is lost.
endings.bad: One or both clients start moving business elsewhere, and engineering is busy fixing promises made in a hurry.

steps.msg: Ben: 'Client A is a large payments company and wants API access to account data. Client B is a retail chain and wants multi-user approvals for payments. Both threaten to leave. Engineering has capacity for only one this quarter.'

options.t: Ask Ben to set up calls with both clients to learn the exact problem, the deadline and what they would accept as a first step.
options.c: Сначала выясняет реальную потребность каждого клиента.
options.r: Both clients feel heard, and you learn that they need less than they first asked for.

options.t: Choose Client A because the API deal is bigger, and tell Client B they will wait.
options.c: Выбор по размеру сделки, без проверки потребностей.
options.r: Client A is happy, but Client B feels ignored and starts looking at other banks.

options.t: Promise both clients delivery this quarter, and ask engineering to find a way.
options.c: Невыполнимое обещание подорвёт доверие обоих.
options.r: Engineering is overloaded, and both clients will soon face missed promises.

options.t: Ask Ben which client renews first, and focus on that client.
options.c: Разумный критерий, но без разговора с клиентами его мало.
options.r: You get a rough order, but you still do not know what each client really needs.

words.how: Момент, когда клиент решает, остаться ли с банком.
words.ex: Client B's renewal is in March.
Engineering has capacity for one request.

steps.msg: After the calls: Client A needs read-only access to transaction data for one partner. Client B needs two approvers for payments above 10,000. Engineering says each can be built as a small version in four weeks.
steps.alt: The calls were tense and Ben is nervous. Client A needs read-only access to transaction data for one partner, and Client B needs two approvers for payments above 10,000. Engineering says each can be built as a small version in four weeks.

options.t: Build both small versions in sequence: Client B's approvals first because its renewal is sooner, then Client A's read-only API.
options.c: Делит работу на малые части и учитывает сроки продления.
options.r: Both clients get a date and a clear first version, and engineering stays focused.

options.t: Build Client A's API first with the full feature set, and leave Client B's approvals for next year.
options.c: Теряет клиента B и берёт лишнюю работу.
options.r: Client A is delighted, but Client B moves part of its business to another bank.

options.t: Build neither until a bigger customer survey shows demand across the market.
options.c: Откладывает решение, пока клиенты уходят.
options.r: Both clients lose patience, and engineering has nothing clear to work on.

options.t: Build only Client B's approvals now, and tell Client A that its request comes in the second half of the year.
options.c: Реалистично, но возможность сделать обе малые версии упущена.
options.r: Client B is happy and Client A waits, but the late request returns and interrupts engineering.

words.how: Можно смотреть данные, но нельзя менять.
Человек, который подтверждает платёж или решение.
words.ex: Two approvers must confirm large payments.

steps.msg: Four weeks in, Client B's approvals are almost ready, but compliance finds that the feature needs an audit log of who approved what. This adds two weeks.

options.t: Add the audit log, tell Client B about the two extra weeks and the reason, and offer to start a pilot with one team meanwhile.
options.c: Объясняет причину, сохраняет качество и даёт клиенту пилот.
options.r: Client B values the honesty, starts a small pilot and becomes a strong supporter.

options.t: Skip the audit log for now and ship on time, adding it in a second release.
options.c: Нарушает требования комплаенса и ведёт к переделкам.
options.r: Client B is pleased with the speed, but compliance blocks the launch and engineering rushes to fix it.

options.t: Tell Client B nothing and keep the date, hoping the extra work fits in the schedule.
options.c: Молчание о задержке разрушает доверие.
options.r: The date slips, and Client B learns about it from its own team, not from you.

options.t: Add the audit log and share the new date in the weekly update, without offering any interim step.
options.c: Честно, но клиент остаётся без решения на две недели.
options.r: Client B accepts the delay, but it waits two weeks with nothing to use.

words.how: Запись о том, кто и что сделал в системе.
words.ex: The audit log shows who approved the payment.

words.how: Отдел или процесс, который следит за выполнением правил и законов.

steps.msg: Client B is live. Client A now asks if it can have the read-only API this quarter after all, because a competitor bank offered it.

options.t: Share the plan: the read-only API is next, with a date and one clear first use case, and invite Client A to test it early.
options.c: Даёт понятный план и вовлекает клиента.
options.r: Client A stays, joins early testing, and its feedback shapes the API.

options.t: Say the API will come eventually, and avoid giving dates.
options.c: Без дат клиент не может планировать.
options.r: Client A feels unimportant and starts talks with the competitor.

options.t: Promise an API with all features immediately, even though the team has not designed it.
options.c: Громкое обещание без проекта опасно.
options.r: The team is rushed, and the first version has serious security gaps.

options.t: Offer a data export as a file for now, and promise the API later.
options.c: Помогает на время, но задачу API не решает.
options.r: Client A accepts the file export as a short-term bridge, but it still pushes for the API.

words.how: Конкретная ситуация, в которой клиент использует продукт.
words.ex: The first use case is partner reporting.
A file export is an interim solution.

endings.good: Activation climbs from 30% to nearly 60% without breaking the budget. Leo says you have a gift for finding the real problem, and the team learns a method it can repeat.
endings.mid: Activation improves, but part of the budget and time goes to things that did not matter much. The team sees progress, and the CEO wants a clearer plan next time.
endings.bad: The budget is nearly gone and activation barely moves. Leadership starts asking whether account opening is a priority at all.

steps.msg: Only 30% of new customers finish opening an account in the Northwind app. We have a small budget and one engineer for a month. Where do you start?

options.t: Look at the funnel to find the biggest drop-off step, and watch session recordings of customers who quit there.
options.c: Находит, где именно теряются клиенты, почти бесплатно.
options.r: You find that most people quit at the ID photo step. The team now has a clear target at no cost.

options.t: Hire an agency to redesign the whole account opening flow from scratch, with a new look and new steps.
options.c: Дорого и долго, а причина падения неизвестна.
options.r: The redesign eats the budget and a month of engineering, and nobody knows whether it fixes the real problem.

options.t: Send a push notification promising a 10 dollar bonus to anyone who finishes, and leave the flow untouched.
options.c: Платит за результат, не разобравшись в причине ухода.
options.r: A few more people finish, but most still quit at the same step, and the bonus costs real money.

options.t: Run a short in-app survey asking customers why they stopped, and decide after the answers arrive.
options.c: Полезно, но ответов мало и ждать долго: данные воронки быстрее.
options.r: Only a few customers reply and the answers are vague, but they give some hints.

words.how: Шаги, которые проходит клиент, и доля людей, доходящих до каждого.
words.ex: The funnel shows where customers quit.
The biggest drop-off is at the ID photo.

steps.msg: The data shows 45% of customers quit at the ID photo step. Interviews say people don't trust the app with their documents yet.
steps.alt: Your first fix barely helped. The data shows 45% of customers quit at the ID photo step, and interviews say people don't trust the app with their documents yet.

options.t: Move the ID step later, and let customers explore the app with a demo account so they see the value before sharing documents.
options.c: Решает причину недоверия: сначала ценность, потом документы.
options.r: Customers reach their first success before they are asked for documents, and more of them continue.

options.t: Add a short text about data security next to the ID photo button, and keep the step in the same place.
options.c: Небольшое улучшение, но шаг остаётся ранним и пугающим.
options.r: A small improvement, but the step is still early and scary.

options.t: Add a warning that the application will be cancelled in 24 hours without the ID photo.
options.c: Давление усиливает страх, и люди уходят.
options.r: More customers feel pressured and leave the app.

options.t: Keep the ID step where it is, but add a short video that explains how documents are stored and protected.
options.c: Снижает тревогу, но видео смотрят немногие.
options.r: Some customers watch the video and continue, but most still quit at the same place.

words.how: Пробный счёт с примерами, чтобы увидеть ценность продукта.
words.ex: A demo account shows the value quickly.
Customers need trust before sharing documents.

steps.msg: The new order is live. Activation rose from 30% to 41% in two weeks. The CEO asks if you can reach 60% by the end of the quarter, but the budget is almost gone.

options.t: Pick the next biggest drop-off from the funnel, fix it with a small change, and test it on half of new customers first.
options.c: Следующий шаг делается дёшево и проверяется на части клиентов.
options.r: The next fix is cheap, the test confirms it works, and activation keeps climbing.

options.t: Ask the team to work evenings for three weeks and fix every remaining issue at once.
options.c: Перегружает команду и не показывает, что сработало.
options.r: The team burns out fast, and nobody can tell which change helped.

options.t: Tell the CEO that 41% is enough, since the main problem is solved, and stop working on onboarding.
options.c: Останавливается раньше цели и теряет поддержку.
options.r: Leadership sees the target slip away, and the momentum disappears.

options.t: Ask the CEO for extra budget to buy ads that bring more new customers into the same flow.
options.c: Больше людей на входе, но воронка прежняя.
options.r: Traffic grows and a few more customers finish, but the extra spend is not matched by results.

words.how: Правка, которую можно сделать быстро и дёшево.
words.ex: A small change can move the metric.
We tested it on half of new customers.

steps.msg: Two weeks later, activation is at 52%. Support reports that customers keep asking the same three questions about the ID photo. What do you do next?

options.t: Add short answers to those three questions inside the app next to the step, and track whether support tickets drop.
options.c: Закрывает реальные вопросы клиентов и измеряет результат.
options.r: Tickets about the ID photo drop by half, and activation reaches 58%.

options.t: Build a full chatbot for account opening, and plan the launch for next quarter.
options.c: Решение большое и дорогое, а вопросов всего три.
options.r: The chatbot takes months and loads the team while the simple questions stay unanswered.

options.t: Ignore the questions, since activation is already above 50% and the target is close.
options.c: Лёгкая победа упущена, клиенты продолжают уходить.
options.r: The same questions keep coming, and some customers quit at the step.

options.t: Ask support to answer these questions in chat faster, and review the numbers again next month.
options.c: Помогает, но причину вопросов не убирает.
options.r: Chats get faster replies, but the questions keep arriving and the step stays unclear.

words.how: Запрос клиента, записанный в системе поддержки.
words.ex: Support tickets show what confuses customers.

words.how: Доля новых клиентов, дошедших до ценности продукта.
words.ex: The activation rate went up to 52%.

sender.name: Anna
sender.role: Account Manager at the card processor

endings.good: The bank pays far less than the first demand and keeps a strong relationship with its processor. Finance is impressed, and you have the flexibility to review the deal after a year.
endings.mid: The deal is acceptable, but the bank gives up some flexibility or goodwill along the way.
endings.bad: The bank ends up with a worse deal and a cold relationship. The CEO questions the way vendors are managed.

steps.msg: Anna from our card processor writes: 'From next quarter, processing fees will increase by 25%. This is standard for all clients.' Your bank depends on this vendor for every card payment.

options.t: Reply politely, ask for the reasons behind the increase, and prepare data on your volume and growth to discuss a better deal and a longer-term plan.
options.c: Собирает аргументы и готовит разговор.
options.r: Anna agrees to a call, and you arrive with numbers that support your position.

options.t: Offer a three-year contract in exchange for a smaller increase of 10%.
options.c: Снижает цену, но привязывает банк к одному поставщику.
options.r: The price is lower, but the bank is locked in, and switching later becomes expensive.

options.t: Threaten to switch to another processor immediately.
options.c: Угроза без альтернативы выглядит как блеф.
options.r: Anna calls your bluff, since the bank has no tested alternative, and the relationship cools.

options.t: Ask Anna for a call, and say the increase is hard for your budget.
options.c: Вежливо, но без аргументов и предложений.
options.r: Anna agrees to talk, but she expects numbers, and you have none ready.

words.how: Плата поставщику за обработку каждой операции.
words.ex: Processing fees will go up by 25%.

words.how: Ситуация, когда сменить партнёра очень дорого.

steps.msg: On the call, Anna says she cannot cut the fee, but she may offer a volume discount or extra services. Your finance team says every percent counts.
steps.alt: The call starts coldly. Anna says she cannot cut the fee, but she may offer a volume discount or extra services. Your finance team says every percent counts.

options.t: Ask for a tiered discount linked to your volume, and a clause that lets the bank adjust or leave if service quality drops.
options.c: Привязывает скидку к объёму и сохраняет свободу.
options.r: Anna agrees to explore tiers, and the quality clause gives the bank an exit if service drops.

options.t: Accept the extra services she offers, even if the bank does not need them.
options.c: Платит за ненужное и теряет деньги.
options.r: The extra services add cost, and the bank barely uses them.

options.t: Say the offer is insulting, and end the call.
options.c: Разрыв разговора портит отношения.
options.r: Anna stops returning your emails, and the relationship turns cold.

options.t: Ask for a volume discount only, and accept the standard contract terms otherwise.
options.c: Хорошо, но без защитных условий.
options.r: You win a small discount, but the bank gets no protection if service quality drops.

words.how: Снижение цены при большом количестве операций.
words.ex: We asked for a volume discount.
A tiered discount grows with volume.

steps.msg: Anna offers a final deal: a 12% increase instead of 25%, a two-year term, and a clause for review after one year. The CEO wants an answer this week.

options.t: Accept after a quick check with finance and legal, and ask to add a service-quality clause. Thank Anna for her flexibility.
options.c: Быстро проверяет условия и сохраняет отношения.
options.r: The deal is signed with a quality clause, and Anna remembers the respect.

options.t: Counter once more with an 8% increase, and refuse to move if she says no.
options.c: Жёсткая позиция может сорвать почти готовую сделку.
options.r: Anna refuses, and you end up with the 25% increase after all.

options.t: Reject the deal and announce that the bank will switch to another processor.
options.c: Резкий разрыв без запасного варианта слишком рискован.
options.r: The switch takes months, and the bank pays more in the meantime.

options.t: Accept the deal immediately without checking with finance or legal.
options.c: Быстро, но без проверки рисков.
options.r: The deal is signed, but legal finds an unfavorable clause a week later.

endings.good: The team trusts you, the product's decline slows, and leadership sees a PM who listens, learns and delivers. Nora says you earned your place.
endings.mid: Things improve slowly, but the team and leadership are still not fully convinced. You have a good start and more to prove.
endings.bad: The team pulls back, leadership loses patience, and the product keeps declining. You will need to rebuild trust before anything else.

steps.msg: It is your first week as PM of Northwind's savings product, which has been losing customers for two quarters. The team is wary, and Nora asks how you will start.

options.t: Meet each team member one-on-one, listen to what they think is wrong, and review customer feedback and data before making any plan.
options.c: Слушает команду и изучает данные до решений.
options.r: The team opens up, and you learn things no report shows.

options.t: Present a new vision to the team on day two, so everyone sees you have a plan.
options.c: План без знаний выглядит самоуверенно.
options.r: The team nods politely, but they feel you do not yet understand the product.

options.t: Replace the existing roadmap with your own plan, and tell the team to follow it.
options.c: Ломает доверие и пренебрегает опытом команды.
options.r: The team stops sharing ideas, and two people ask about moving to other teams.

options.t: Join the daily meetings and observe quietly for two weeks before speaking.
options.c: Много узнаёт, но молчание можно принять за безразличие.
options.r: You learn a lot, but the team starts to wonder whether you care.

words.how: Разговор двух людей без других участников.
words.ex: I had a one-on-one with every engineer.

words.how: Получить продукт или проблему от предшественника.
words.ex: You inherited a product in decline.

steps.msg: Team members say customers leave because the interest rate is no longer competitive, and because transfers to other banks are slow. Nora asks which one you will tackle first.
steps.alt: The team is still guarded. They say customers leave because the interest rate is no longer competitive, and because transfers to other banks are slow. Nora asks which one you will tackle first.

options.t: Compare both with data: how many customers left for each reason and what each fix would cost. Then choose the cheaper, faster fix first.
options.c: Выбирает по данным и стоимости.
options.r: The data points to slow transfers as the cheaper fix, and the team agrees with the logic.

options.t: Fix the interest rate first, since customers mention it most, without checking the data.
options.c: Самая частая жалоба не всегда самая важная.
options.r: The rate change is costly, and the numbers show it was not the main reason for leaving.

options.t: Take on both fixes at once and promise results in a month.
options.c: Две задачи сразу и громкое обещание.
options.r: The team spreads thin, and the promise is missed.

options.t: Fix transfers first because it is a technical change the team can do quickly.
options.c: Быстро, но без сравнения причин по данным.
options.r: The fix is fast, but you do not know whether it is the biggest reason customers leave.

words.how: Процентная ставка не хуже, чем у других банков.
words.ex: The rate is no longer competitive.

steps.msg: The head of retail banking asks for a clear plan, since the product is losing money. He wants quick wins and a long-term path.

options.t: Present a 90-day plan with two quick wins and one longer bet, with metrics and risks, and agree on a monthly review.
options.c: Совмещает быстрые победы и долгосрочный план.
options.r: He approves the plan, and the monthly review gives him visibility.

options.t: Say it is too early to promise anything, and ask for six months.
options.c: Честно, но без конкретики руководитель теряет терпение.
options.r: He grows impatient, and he asks someone else to prepare a plan.

options.t: Promise to double customer growth in three months, to calm him down.
options.c: Невыполнимое обещание сработает против вас.
options.r: He is calm for a week, then the missed promise damages your credibility.

options.t: Present quick wins only, and leave the longer plan for later.
options.c: Хорошо для скорости, но направление пока неясно.
options.r: He likes the quick wins but asks what happens after the first quarter.

words.how: Идея с высоким риском и потенциалом.
words.ex: One longer bet is enough for now.

steps.msg: A quick win fails: the new transfer speed is faster, but customers do not notice. The head of retail asks what went wrong.

options.t: Explain what you learned: the change was real but not visible, show how you will test the message with customers, and propose the next step.
options.c: Признаёт урок и предлагает следующий шаг.
options.r: He sees a PM who learns fast, and he supports your next test.

options.t: Say that the team did everything right and that customers simply do not understand the improvement.
options.c: Винит клиентов вместо анализа.
options.r: He feels you are defensive, and the team learns nothing.

options.t: Blame the previous PM's decisions and the poor state of the product you inherited.
options.c: Перекладывание вины на предшественника.
options.r: He sees an excuse, and the team stops trusting your judgment.

options.t: Say you will look into it and come back with an answer next week.
options.c: Вежливо, но без позиции.
options.r: He waits, but he expected at least a first hypothesis.

words.ex: Customers did not notice the perceived value.
The lesson learned is to test the message.

steps.msg: After three months, customer losses slow and the team seems more confident. Nora asks how you will keep the momentum.

options.t: Share the results openly, credit the team's ideas, and set the next quarter's goals together with the team and retail banking.
options.c: Делится успехом и вовлекает людей в цели.
options.r: The team feels ownership, and leadership sees a stable path.

options.t: Keep going as is, and avoid new commitments to protect the progress.
options.c: Осторожно, но без движения вперёд.
options.r: Progress stalls, and leadership asks what comes next.

options.t: Take credit for the results at the leadership meeting, and announce the next big plan.
options.c: Присваивает успех и теряет команду.
options.r: The team hears about it and feels used, and momentum drops.

options.t: Present the results to leadership with the team's names, and plan the next quarter yourself.
options.c: Хорошо отмечает команду, но цели ставит один.
options.r: The team feels recognized but not involved, and ownership stays weak.

words.ex: We need to keep the momentum.
Give the team credit for the result.

endings.good: Customers and regulators see a bank that acts quickly and honestly. Trust recovers, and the new process makes releases safer for everyone.
endings.mid: The incident is handled, but a few weak spots in communication or process remain. The regulator is watching closely.
endings.bad: The incident becomes a story about secrecy. Customers leave, the regulator opens a formal review, and the team spends months on damage control.

steps.msg: Hannah: 'A release bug showed the names and partial account numbers of about 2,300 customers to other customers for six hours. The bug is fixed now. What do you do first?'

options.t: Form an incident team with compliance, security and support, confirm exactly who was affected, and prepare the notifications to the regulator and to affected customers.
options.c: Устанавливает факты и готовит обязательные уведомления.
options.r: Facts are clear within hours, and the bank notifies the regulator and customers on time.

options.t: Wait a few days to collect more details before telling anyone, so the report is complete.
options.c: Ожидание рискует нарушить сроки уведомления.
options.r: The notification deadline gets closer, and an employee leaks the story before the bank speaks.

options.t: Keep it internal because the bug is fixed and the data was only partial.
options.c: Сокрытие инцидента хуже, когда он всплывёт.
options.r: A customer posts a screenshot, and the bank looks like it tried to hide the incident.

options.t: Notify affected customers quickly with a short message, and prepare the regulator report afterwards.
options.c: Быстро, но регулятор должен узнать вовремя.
options.r: Customers appreciate the speed, but the regulator asks why it learned about the incident later.

words.ex: The bank sent a notification to affected customers.

words.how: Орган, который контролирует банки и их правила.
words.ex: The regulator must be informed in time.

steps.msg: Support is flooded with calls. The CEO wants a public statement by tomorrow. Hannah says the message must be accurate and cannot promise things the bank cannot guarantee.
steps.alt: A rumor has already started online. Support is flooded with calls, and the CEO wants a public statement by tomorrow. Hannah says the message must be accurate and cannot promise things the bank cannot guarantee.

options.t: Publish a clear, honest statement: what happened, which data was visible, what the bank did, and what customers should do. Prepare simple scripts for support.
options.c: Ясно, честно и практично для клиентов и поддержки.
options.r: Customers see the facts and the next steps, and the number of calls starts to fall.

options.t: Publish a short statement that says there was a technical issue and the bank is investigating.
options.c: Слишком общо: клиенты хотят знать, что с их данными.
options.r: The statement raises more questions than it answers, and the calls continue.

options.t: Promise that no customer will suffer any loss and that this will never happen again.
options.c: Обещания, которые банк не может гарантировать, опасны.
options.r: A later fraud attempt appears, and the promise is quoted back to the bank.

options.t: Send the statement only to affected customers by email, and leave the public website without news.
options.c: Правильно для затронутых, но остальные узнают из слухов.
options.r: Affected customers are informed, but others hear rumors and lose trust.

steps.msg: The root cause: a new caching feature skipped a permissions check, and the privacy review for that release was cut to save time. Hannah asks what will change in the release process.

options.t: Make privacy review a required gate for any release that touches customer data, add automated permission tests, and set clear owners.
options.c: Меняет процесс, а не только чинит ошибку.
options.r: The next releases are slightly slower, but they are safer, and the regulator notes your corrective steps.

options.t: Add a reminder to the release checklist and ask engineers to be more careful.
options.c: Напоминание без проверок не защищает.
options.r: The reminder is forgotten within a month.

options.t: Remove the person who approved the release from the team, and consider the matter closed.
options.c: Наказание не исправляет процесс.
options.r: The team becomes afraid of mistakes, and the process stays as weak as before.

options.t: Add automated permission tests only, and keep privacy review optional for urgent releases.
options.c: Хорошо, но исключение для срочных релизов оставляет дыру.
options.r: Tests catch many problems, but the next urgent release skips review again.

words.how: Шаг, без которого релиз не может идти дальше.
words.ex: Privacy review is now a gate.

words.how: Проверка того, кому разрешено видеть данные.
words.ex: The release skipped a permission check.

steps.msg: Hannah asks you to present the incident to the board: what happened, what it cost, and how the bank will prevent it. The board is worried and wants clear answers.

options.t: Present facts and numbers, own the mistake, show the corrective plan with owners and dates, and propose a quarterly privacy audit.
options.c: Честность, конкретные меры и ответственные.
options.r: The board approves the plan and the extra budget, and respects the way you handled it.

options.t: Present the incident briefly and say it was a one-time problem that is unlikely to repeat.
options.c: Недооценка риска без плана выглядит безответственно.
options.r: The board asks hard questions you cannot answer, and trust in the plan drops.

options.t: Blame a vendor library and say the bank had no part in the bug.
options.c: Перекладывание вины вскроется при проверке.
options.r: Regulators find the real cause quickly, and the board sees the bank as unreliable.

options.t: Present the plan without numbers, and promise to share the details in the next report.
options.c: План есть, но без цифр совет не оценит риск.
options.r: The board accepts the plan for now, but asks for the missing numbers within a week.

words.ex: We listed corrective actions with owners.
A quarterly audit will catch gaps.

tone.ctx: You need to tell Dana that Excel export will not make it into Friday's release.

opts.t: Let's ship CSV on Friday and move Excel to next week. Does that work for you?
opts.c: Решение ясное, но звучит как общий план, а вопрос в конце оставляет Дане место для мнения.

opts.t: Excel is out. Ship CSV on Friday and don't start anything else this week.
opts.c: Решение то же, но приказной тон: «Excel is out» и запрет звучат резко и без уважения к работе команды.

opts.t: As I said before, Excel was always risky. Let's just ship CSV, I guess.
opts.c: «As I said before» и «I guess» читаются как упрёк и пассивная агрессия, хотя по сути решение верное.

b01.build: let's descope excel and ship the csv export on friday

tone.ctx: The VP wants a result today, but the test needs two more weeks. Write a reply to the VP.

opts.t: We need about two more weeks to be sure. I'll send you the final result on the 14th.
opts.c: Спокойно объясняет причину и даёт конкретную дату, поэтому VP слышит уверенность, а не отказ.

opts.t: Four days is not enough data. You'll get an answer when the test is done.
opts.c: По сути верно, но звучит как поучение руководителя и без конкретного срока.

opts.t: Sorry, I'm not really sure yet, maybe we could wait a bit if that's okay?
opts.c: Слишком много извинений и «maybe»: звучит неуверенно, и VP не получает ни решения, ни даты.

b03.build: keep the test running until we reach statistical significance

tone.ctx: The team is excited to start building after five interviews. You want to test pricing first.

opts.t: Great signal from the interviews! Before we build, let's check if people will actually pay.
opts.c: Сначала признаёт работу команды, потом предлагает следующий шаг через «let's», без давления.

opts.t: Five interviews prove nothing. Nobody starts building until I say so.
opts.c: Обесценивает интервью и звучит как приказ «until I say so», команда потеряет мотивацию.

opts.t: Sure, let's build it, if we're fine with guessing what people will pay.
opts.c: Формально соглашается, но сарказм «if we're fine with guessing» звучит как пассивная агрессия.

b04.build: test willingness to pay with a pricing page experiment first

tone.ctx: DAU dropped after Tuesday's release. You need data from the engineering team.

opts.t: Could you share the Tuesday release notes? I want to rule it out as a possible cause.
opts.c: Просит о конкретном и объясняет зачем, никого не обвиняя: «rule it out» звучит нейтрально.

opts.t: Your Tuesday release probably broke DAU. Send me the release notes now.
opts.c: Обвиняет команду без данных и требует «now», люди начнут защищаться, а не помогать.

opts.t: Interesting how DAU dropped right after your release. Any thoughts on that?
opts.c: «Interesting how...» это скрытый упрёк: вопрос звучит как намёк, что виноваты они.

b05.build: segment the drop by cohort to find the root cause

tone.ctx: Marketing changed the requirements for the third time this month. Write to the marketing lead.

opts.t: Can we agree on one owner for requirements? Late changes are hard on the design team.
opts.c: Предлагает решение и спокойно называет последствия, без обвинения конкретного человека.

opts.t: Stop changing the requirements. Design can't keep redoing your work.
opts.c: «Stop» и «your work» звучат как обвинение, маркетинг начнёт оправдываться.

opts.t: Third change this month, nice. I'm sure design will love it again.
opts.c: Чистый сарказм: «nice» и «will love it» это пассивная агрессия, которая портит отношения.

b06.build: name one owner for requirements and add a sign off step

tone.ctx: Support says they aren't ready for next week's launch. Reply to the support lead.

opts.t: Thanks for flagging this early. Let's go through the checklist together today.
opts.c: Благодарит за сигнал и предлагает совместный конкретный шаг, это тон партнёра.

opts.t: The date is announced, so support just has to be ready. No excuses.
opts.c: Игнорирует проблему и звучит как давление, «No excuses» особенно резко.

opts.t: I'm so sorry, this is all my fault. We can do whatever you think is best.
opts.c: Слишком много вины и ноль решений: PM отдаёт решение и выглядит неуверенно.

b07.build: run the readiness checklist with support then pick a phased rollout

tone.ctx: The sales team's request didn't make the top three this quarter. Tell the sales lead.

opts.t: Your request didn't make the top three this quarter. Happy to walk you through the scoring.
opts.c: Честно говорит «нет» и сразу предлагает объяснить логику, отказ звучит справедливо.

opts.t: Your request is out. The scoring says it's not important enough.
opts.c: «Is out» и «not important enough» звучат пренебрежительно к работе отдела продаж.

opts.t: We'll see, maybe it gets in at some point. Hard to say right now.
opts.c: Размытый ответ: создаёт ложную надежду, и через месяц будет тот же разговор.

b08.build: score all twelve requests by impact and effort

tone.ctx: Maya wants to call her campaign a win, but retention is flat. Write to Maya.

opts.t: The signup growth is great work. Let's also show retention, so the board sees the full picture.
opts.c: Признаёт результат Майи и предлагает добавить контекст, а не спорить с ней.

opts.t: You can't call this a win. Retention is flat, so the campaign didn't work.
opts.c: Обесценивает работу целиком, хотя рост регистраций реален. Звучит как приговор.

opts.t: Sure, call it a win, as long as nobody on the board looks at retention.
opts.c: Сарказм вместо аргумента: Майя услышит насмешку, а не риск.

b11.build: report the growth but flag flat retention as a risk

tone.ctx: Leo suggests removing step 3 of onboarding. You want to check the data first.

opts.t: Good idea to look at step 3. Before we remove it, can we check the recordings together?
opts.c: Поддерживает фокус Лео и превращает спор в совместную проверку.

opts.t: We're not removing step 3. Some customers need it, so drop the idea.
opts.c: Закрывает идею без обсуждения, «drop the idea» звучит грубо.

opts.t: Removing it is one option, if we don't care about the customers who use it.
opts.c: Намекает, что Лео не думает о клиентах: это пассивная агрессия.

b12.build: watch session recordings then test a version where the import is deferred

tone.ctx: Zoe collected ten dark mode requests and thinks it's a must-have. Reply to Zoe.

opts.t: Thanks for collecting these! I'll compare dark mode with other priorities and get back to you.
opts.c: Ценит работу Зои и обещает понятный следующий шаг, не обещая результат.

opts.t: Ten requests is nothing. Dark mode is not happening this quarter.
opts.c: Обесценивает сигнал и решает без анализа, Зоя перестанет приносить запросы.

opts.t: Ten whole requests, wow. I'll add it to the list with everything else.
opts.c: «Ten whole requests, wow» это насмешка, хотя смысл ответа нормальный.

b16.build: rank dark mode against other opportunities by impact

tone.ctx: In an interview, a user asks for an export button. You want to find the real problem.

opts.t: That's really helpful. Could you show me what you do with the table after you copy it?
opts.c: Мягко благодарит и просит показать процесс, пользователь охотно раскроет настоящую задачу.

opts.t: Why do you even need export? Just tell me what problem you have.
opts.c: «Why do you even need» звучит как допрос, пользователь закроется.

opts.t: Okay, export, got it. Anything else you want us to build for you?
opts.c: Вежливо, но просто записывает запрос и не ищет проблему, интервью теряет смысл.

b24.build: ask what underlying problem they solve with this workaround

tone.ctx: The CEO is delighted about a sudden signup spike. You want to check the data first.

opts.t: Exciting numbers! Let me check the source first, so we're sure the spike is real.
opts.c: Разделяет радость и спокойно объясняет проверку, CEO не почувствует себя глупо.

opts.t: Don't get excited. This is probably bots or a tracking bug.
opts.c: Звучит как запрет радоваться и обрывает CEO, хотя проверка действительно нужна.

opts.t: Sure, let's celebrate, unless it turns out to be bots again.
opts.c: «Again» и «sure, let's celebrate» читаются как подкол, это пассивная агрессия.

b52.build: verify the source before we celebrate the spike

tone.ctx: Support tickets about 'missing steps' went up after the new onboarding. Reply to support.

opts.t: Thanks for the ticket data. Let's add a short guide to the new flow and review tickets weekly.
opts.c: Благодарит, предлагает конкретное действие и регулярную проверку, поддержка чувствует, что её слышат.

opts.t: The tickets are just users getting used to it. Ignore them for now.
opts.c: Отмахивается от сигнала поддержки, «ignore them» звучит пренебрежительно.

opts.t: I guess users can't handle a small change. We'll add a guide if we really have to.
opts.c: «I guess users can't handle» и «if we really have to» это раздражение и пассивная агрессия.

sc07.build: ship the minimum version behind a feature flag

tone.ctx: A big client wants a custom dashboard on this quarter's roadmap, and Mark is pushing you to say yes. Write your reply to Mark.

opts.t: I understand the renewal matters. Let me find out what the dashboard is for, and I'll send you a scoped option by Friday.
opts.c: Показывает, что ты понял важность сделки, и даёт конкретный следующий шаг со сроком.

opts.t: The roadmap is full. I can't add anything, so the client will have to wait.
opts.c: Жёсткий отказ без вопросов и без альтернативы: Mark почувствует, что его проблему игнорируют.

opts.t: Okay, I'll try to somehow fit it in, but I can't promise anything, sorry.
opts.c: Слишком много «try» и «sorry»: звучит неуверенно, а обещание «как-нибудь втиснуть» опасно.

b02.build: let me find out what the dashboard is for first

tone.ctx: Anna offers a 10% discount for a two-year contract, but your budget is tight. Write your reply.

opts.t: Thank you for the offer. Two years is a long commitment for us. Could we keep the discount with an opt-out clause after year one?
opts.c: Вежливо благодарит, называет возражение и предлагает конкретное условие.

opts.t: Ten percent is too small. Give us thirty or we walk away.
opts.c: Ультиматум закрывает переговоры, и Anna вряд ли захочет искать компромисс.

opts.t: Fine, whatever you think is best, we'll sign the two years.
opts.c: Мгновенное согласие отдаёт все рычаги, а «whatever» звучит безразлично.

b09.build: could we keep the discount with an opt-out clause after year one

tone.ctx: Ben wants to promise feature X to a client today, but engineering has not finished the estimate. Write your reply to Ben.

opts.t: I can't commit to a date yet. It's planned for Q4, and I'll confirm timing next week once the estimate is done.
opts.c: Честно говорит, что даты пока нет, даёт ориентир и срок подтверждения.

opts.t: Don't promise anything. It's not your call, and dates are my job.
opts.c: Сухо и резко: Ben получает запрет без объяснения и без помощи с клиентом.

opts.t: Probably December? I'm not sure, but you can say it, I guess.
opts.c: «Probably» и «I guess» превращаются в обещание клиенту, которое потом придётся нарушить.

b10.build: it is planned for q4 and the date is still tentative

tone.ctx: Nora asks how the team will measure success of the 'improve onboarding' objective. Write your reply.

opts.t: Good question. I suggest we raise activation from 35% to 50% this quarter, and I'll share the full list of key results by Wednesday.
opts.c: Называет метрику, базу и цель и обещает срок, поэтому ответ конкретный и проверяемый.

opts.t: We'll know it when we see it. Onboarding is clearly better now, so just trust the team.
opts.c: «Trust the team» уходит от вопроса, а измерить успех без цифр нельзя.

opts.t: Maybe something like more users finishing it? I haven't really thought about it, sorry.
opts.c: Размытая формулировка и извинение: Nora не получит ни метрики, ни плана.

b14.build: raise activation from thirty five to fifty percent this quarter

tone.ctx: Dana says priorities changed three times this month and the team is frustrated. Write your reply.

opts.t: You're right, and I'm sorry for the disruption. Let's set up a weekly priority review, and any urgent work will replace something instead of adding to the sprint.
opts.c: Признаёт проблему, не ищет виноватых и предлагает понятное правило.

opts.t: Priorities change because the business changes. The team needs to be more flexible.
opts.c: Перекладывает вину на команду и обесценивает её усталость.

opts.t: It's not really my fault, the VP of Sales keeps asking, so what can I do?
opts.c: Оправдание и перевод стрелок: решения нет, а Dana остаётся без поддержки.

b22.build: urgent work will replace something instead of adding to the sprint

tone.ctx: The test shows conversion up 3%, but support tickets rose 15%. The sponsor wants to ship. Write your reply to the sponsor.

opts.t: The conversion gain looks good, but tickets rose 15%. Let me find out why before we ship, so we don't grow with confused users.
opts.c: Признаёт плюс, называет риск и предлагает конкретный шаг без давления на спонсора.

opts.t: Tickets don't matter. Conversion is up, so let's ship it today.
opts.c: Игнорирует тревожный сигнал: рост конверсии может быть за счёт запутавшихся пользователей.

opts.t: Hmm, I think maybe we should wait, but I'm not sure, what do you think?
opts.c: Сомнение без аргументов и вопрос в конце перекладывают решение на спонсора.

b23.build: let me find out why tickets rose before we ship

tone.ctx: The launch email goes out tomorrow, but legal has not approved the pricing wording. Write your message to the team.

opts.t: Legal hasn't approved the pricing wording yet. I'll call them today, and I'm preparing a version without prices in case we miss the deadline.
opts.c: Сообщает факт, называет действие на сегодня и запасной вариант.

opts.t: Legal is blocking us again. Somebody needs to push them, or we'll miss the launch.
opts.c: Обвиняет юристов, не предлагает плана, и команда начнёт искать виноватого.

opts.t: We might have a small problem with the email, but maybe it will be fine, hopefully.
opts.c: «Maybe» и «hopefully»: проблема размыта, и команда не понимает, что делать.

b25.build: i will call legal today and prepare a version without prices

tone.ctx: QA found a minor bug a day before release; the release is tied to a client announcement. Write your update to the stakeholders.

opts.t: QA found a bug that affects about 2% of users, and there's a workaround. I recommend we ship on time and fix it in a patch next week.
opts.c: Даёт масштаб, говорит про обходной путь и предлагает решение с планом исправления.

opts.t: There's a bug, but nobody will notice it. We're shipping, end of discussion.
opts.c: Закрывает обсуждение и скрывает риск: так теряют доверие.

opts.t: A bug appeared, so I guess we should probably delay, if that's okay with everyone?
opts.c: Нерешительно: отложить релиз ради малого бага вряд ли нужно, и решения нет.

b31.build: we ship on time and fix the bug in a patch next week

tone.ctx: Four of five users could not find the Save button, but Oleg thinks the layout is obvious. Write your reply to Oleg.

opts.t: Four of five users couldn't find it, so let's try a more visible placement and retest with new people.
opts.c: Опирается на факты теста и предлагает проверяемый эксперимент вместе с дизайнером.

opts.t: The users are right and you're wrong. Change the button today.
opts.c: Противопоставляет дизайнеру пользователей и приказывает: Oleg обидится.

opts.t: Maybe the design is fine and the users were tired? I don't know, honestly.
opts.c: Обесценивает данные теста, и проблема так и останется.

b41.build: let us try a more visible placement and retest with new users

tone.ctx: Checkout is failing for 5% of users, and customers are posting about it. Write the update for customers.

opts.t: We found the issue and rolled back the release. Checkout is working again, and we'll share an update with a timeline within the hour.
opts.c: Сообщает факт, статус и конкретный срок следующего апдейта.

opts.t: A small number of users had problems. It's not a big deal and nothing else to say.
opts.c: Преуменьшает проблему, и недовольство клиентов только вырастет.

opts.t: We're really, really sorry, we don't know what happened yet, maybe it will work soon.
opts.c: Много извинений и никакого срока или плана: клиенты не понимают, чего ждать.

s01.build: we rolled back the release and will share an update within the hour

tone.ctx: Mark says a $500k deal needs feature A this quarter, but engineering is full. Write your reply to Mark.

opts.t: I want to help close this deal. Let me confirm that A is the real blocker and set up a call with the client this week.
opts.c: Поддерживает цель Mark и предлагает проверить факты и поговорить с клиентом.

opts.t: Engineering is full. Feature A is not happening, so please tell the client no.
opts.c: Категоричный отказ без вопросов, поэтому Mark пойдёт к руководству мимо тебя.

opts.t: Okay, I'll tell the team to build feature A, even if it breaks something else.
opts.c: Слепо соглашается на сделку, не взвесив стоимость для команды.

s02.build: let me confirm that feature a is the real blocker for the deal

tone.ctx: Priya asks how to test a 15% price increase safely. Write your reply to Priya.

opts.t: Let's show the new price only to new customers so existing ones aren't affected, then compare conversion with the control group.
opts.c: Конкретный безопасный план: новые клиенты и контрольная группа.

opts.t: Just change the price for everyone next month, like the CEO wants.
opts.c: Игнорирует риск для существующих клиентов и ломает смысл теста.

opts.t: I'm not sure testing is needed, but we could try something, if you think so.
opts.c: Размытый ответ без плана: Priya остаётся без решения.

s03.build: show the new price to new customers only and compare conversion

tone.ctx: Mark wants spending insights stopped before the quarterly meeting. Write your reply to Mark.

opts.t: I hear that business clients ask for statements. Could you name three of them, so I can compare their needs with our insights data?
opts.c: Признаёт запрос клиентов и просит конкретные примеры, чтобы сравнить с данными.

opts.t: Insights will stay. I have data and you only have opinions, so we won't stop it.
opts.c: Звучит как «я прав, ты нет», и Mark перейдёт в оборону.

opts.t: I guess you may be right, maybe we can stop insights, if you really want to.
opts.c: Сдаётся без данных: решение будет принято на чувствах.

sc02.build: could you name three clients who asked for statements

tone.ctx: Ira asks for two sprints to fix tech debt, while sales has promised three features. Write your reply to Ira.

opts.t: The delays are real. Let's quantify what the debt costs us and reserve 20% of every sprint for it, while we still ship the promised features.
opts.c: Признаёт проблему, предлагает измерить её и компромисс, который сохраняет обещания.

opts.t: We don't have time for tech debt this quarter. Maybe next year.
opts.c: Отмахивается от проблемы: долг растёт, и скорость падает дальше.

opts.t: Sure, take two sprints, I'll tell sales we can't deliver, I guess.
opts.c: Соглашается на всё сразу и перекладывает проблему на продажи без плана.

b13.build: we reserve twenty percent of every sprint for tech debt

tone.ctx: Engineering says six weeks, sales promised the client three, and the client cares about the date. Write your message to Tom.

opts.t: Could we look at what drives the six weeks? I'd like to cut scope to what the client really needs by their date.
opts.c: Начинает с вопроса о причине срока и предлагает урезать объём, а не давить на людей.

opts.t: Sales promised three weeks, so engineering has to find a way to do it.
opts.c: Перекладывает чужое обещание на инженеров и давит на них.

opts.t: I guess we could maybe try to speed up a bit, if that's possible for you?
opts.c: Просьба «поторопиться» без плана и объёма: Tom не поймёт, что именно делать.

b18.build: let us cut the scope to what the client needs by their date

tone.ctx: A three-year customer asks why their request isn't on the roadmap. Write your reply.

opts.t: Thank you for the feedback. This quarter we focus on reliability, but your request is logged in our backlog, and I'll update you next month.
opts.c: Благодарит, объясняет приоритет квартала и обещает обновление.

opts.t: It's not on the roadmap because it's not important enough, sorry.
opts.c: Прямо говорит, что запрос неважен, и лояльный клиент почувствует себя ненужным.

opts.t: Maybe we'll do it someday, I'll check, but I can't really say anything, sorry.
opts.c: Расплывчато и неуверенно: нет ни причины, ни срока, ни следующего шага.

b27.build: your request is logged in the backlog and i will update you next month

tone.ctx: Sam wants to announce that conversion improved by 25% after the redesign (4% to 5%). Write your reply to Sam.

opts.t: It's a 25% relative gain, or one percentage point in absolute terms. Let me add the confidence interval so the message is accurate.
opts.c: Уточняет обе цифры и предлагает добавить интервал, не обвиняя руководителя.

opts.t: That number is wrong and misleading. You can't tell the company that.
opts.c: Прямо называет слова CEO неправильными: это унижает и не помогает исправить формулировку.

opts.t: Maybe it's 25%, maybe not, I'm not totally sure how it works, sorry.
opts.c: Неуверенность в цифрах подрывает доверие к тебе как к владельцу метрик.

b32.build: it is a twenty five percent relative gain but one point in absolute terms

tone.ctx: A survey says 80% of users love the app, but usage is dropping. Write your reply to Lena.

opts.t: Thanks, Lena. Only 5% answered, and mostly active users, so let's check who the respondents were and dig into the usage drop.
opts.c: Благодарит за работу и объясняет, почему выборка может искажать картину.

opts.t: The survey is useless. Ignore it and look at usage only.
opts.c: Обесценивает работу исследователя: опрос нужен, но его нужно читать правильно.

opts.t: Great, 80% love it! Let's maybe not worry too much about the usage, I guess.
opts.c: Радуется красивой цифре и игнорирует падение использования.

b36.build: let us check who the respondents were and dig into the usage drop

tone.ctx: Maya wants more budget for paid ads, but few signups become customers. Write your reply to Maya.

opts.t: I'd like to check acquisition cost and payback period first. If the unit economics work, I'll support scaling the spend.
opts.c: Просит данные и обещает поддержку при хороших цифрах, поэтому разговор конструктивный.

opts.t: Ads are a waste of money. We're not adding a single dollar.
opts.c: Категорично и без анализа: Maya почувствует, что её работу списали со счетов.

opts.t: Maybe we could try a bit more budget, but I'm not sure it will work.
opts.c: Деньги тратятся без проверки экономики, на надежде.

b40.build: let us check the payback period before we scale the ad spend

tone.ctx: Your main story is blocked by another team's API change. Write your message to the other team's lead.

story.en: Welcome to Northwind Bank, a bank that is moving fast into mobile banking. Today is your first day as a Product Manager Intern in the app team. Your desk is next to the engineers, your laptop is brand new, and Slack is already blinking. Your first task is waiting.

Three months later, your manager invites you to a meeting room. The app team is happy with your work, and you are promoted. From now on you own small features in the Northwind app, from idea to launch, and people come to you with real questions.
A year has passed. Your features are live, customers know the app, and the savings and payments area needs an owner. The job is yours. Numbers, priorities and trade-offs are now on your shoulders.

Two years in, other teams ask for your opinion before they even start planning. As a Senior PM you lead initiatives across payments, cards and business banking. Your decisions now shape the work of many people.

Northwind Bank is growing fast and needs someone to coach its product managers. As a Group PM, your calendar fills up with roadmap reviews and one-on-ones. You no longer solve every problem yourself, you help others solve theirs.

The Head of Product leaves for a new adventure, and the CEO calls you. Product at Northwind Bank is now yours. Hiring, vision and the executive meeting are part of your week, and every decision is watched closely.
The board invites you to a closed meeting. Northwind Bank needs a Chief Product Officer, and they want you. This is the top of the product ladder, in a business where trust is everything.

roles.en: You are learning the basics of product work: reading data, talking to users and helping the team with small tasks. Most decisions are made by others, and you ask a lot of questions.
roles.ru: Ты изучаешь основы продуктовой работы: читаешь данные, общаешься с пользователями и помогаешь команде с небольшими задачами. Решения чаще принимают другие, а ты задаёшь много вопросов.

roles.en: You own small features from idea to launch. You write requirements, run simple experiments and work with engineers and designers every day. A senior PM reviews your decisions.
roles.ru: Ты ведёшь небольшие фичи от идеи до запуска. Пишешь требования, проводишь простые эксперименты и каждый день работаешь с разработчиками и дизайнерами. Решения проверяет старший PM.

roles.en: You own a product area and its metrics. You set priorities, balance stakeholders and make trade-offs with your team without constant supervision.
roles.ru: Ты отвечаешь за продуктовую область и её метрики. Расставляешь приоритеты, балансируешь интересы стейкхолдеров и принимаешь компромиссные решения без постоянного контроля.

roles.en: You lead complex initiatives across several teams and shape the strategy of your area. You mentor other PMs and influence decisions across the company.
roles.ru: Ты ведёшь сложные инициативы на несколько команд и формируешь стратегию направления. Наставляешь других PM и влияешь на решения по всей компании.

roles.en: You manage a group of PMs and several product areas. You align roadmaps, coach your team and connect product goals with company goals.
roles.ru: Ты управляешь группой PM и несколькими продуктовыми направлениями. Согласуешь роадмапы, развиваешь команду и связываешь цели продукта с целями компании.

roles.en: You lead the whole product organization. You define the product vision, hire and grow PMs, and present priorities to the executive team.
roles.ru: Ты руководишь всей продуктовой организацией. Определяешь видение продукта, нанимаешь и растишь PM и представляешь приоритеты топ-менеджменту.

roles.en: You are responsible for the product strategy of the whole company at the board level. You set the vision, build the product culture and answer for product results.
roles.ru: Ты отвечаешь за продуктовую стратегию всей компании на уровне совета директоров. Задаёшь видение, строишь продуктовую культуру и отвечаешь за результаты продукта.

product.endStory: You started as an intern with a single Slack message and finished in the boardroom as the Chief Product Officer of Northwind Bank. You learned the language of product work, one case at a time. Keep it fresh with random cases, the dictionary and articles.
